source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Speed vs. Verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly to remain competitive, accepting that full verification may be incomplete.
pole_b: Maintain the highest standards of verification before publishing; never publish unverified information regardless of competitive pressure.
policy_text: We must maintain the highest standards of verification. / With the amount of rumour and noise circulating online and on social networks, our role of providing accurate and verified news, via identified and reliable sources, has never been more important.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Editorial Independence / Conscience vs. Institutional Direction
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Follow institutional editorial assignments even when they conflict with personal conscience or judgment.
pole_b: Journalists must speak with an independent voice free of external influence; they cannot be compelled to carry out a task that goes against their conscience.
policy_text: AFP journalists must speak with an independent voice, free of prejudice, bias or external influence. They cannot be obliged to carry out a task that goes against their conscience.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Active Truth-Seeking vs. Appearance of Impartiality
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Report what sources say without publicly interrogating or contradicting them, so as to avoid the appearance of taking sides.
pole_b: Actively challenge sources, verify independently stated facts, and draw attention to inconsistencies and errors — even at the risk of appearing partial.
policy_text: AFP journalists have a duty to seek the truth and not passively report information as it is presented to them. They should challenge their sources and question the facts. / We have a duty to report the news but should draw attention to any inconsistencies and inaccuracies in a newsmaker's comments.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Transparency of Identity vs. Subterfuge for Public Interest or Safety
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Conceal or misrepresent identity as a journalist to obtain information or protect personal safety.
pole_b: Always identify yourself as an AFP journalist; never use subterfuge to gather information.
policy_text: AFP journalists must identify themselves as such. They must not use subterfuge other than in exceptional circumstances with the approval of the news management. / It is forbidden to film or record someone without their knowledge when the story concerns their private life or is in a private location.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Presumption of Innocence vs. Public's Right to Know About Criminal Allegations
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report arrests, charges, and criminal proceedings fully and prominently, accepting that this will create reputational damage even before conviction.
pole_b: Respect the presumption of innocence in all reporting; never suggest that arrest or charge equals guilt, regardless of what the evidence appears to show.
policy_text: We must respect the presumption of innocence and never suggest that because an individual has been arrested or charged that he or she is guilty.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Sensitivity to Victims and Vulnerable People vs. News Value
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Pursue and publish the story fully — including interviews with victims, images of suffering, and footage of children — because the public has a legitimate interest in the full reality of events.
pole_b: Exercise sensitivity and avoid intrusion on private grief; obtain parental consent for children; do not tempt eyewitnesses to take risks; minimise harm to vulnerable people as a priority.
policy_text: AFP journalists must exercise sensitivity when approaching victims or their relatives and avoid intruding on private grief. They must take particular care when interviewing or taking images of children, and whenever possible obtain parental consent.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Balanced Coverage vs. Editorial Refusal to Amplify Harmful or False Speech
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Give equal space to all sides of every issue in the name of balance and impartiality, including views that contradict established facts or constitute hate speech.
pole_b: Balance does not require equal space for all views; editors may make judgments about what merits coverage, and are not obliged to repeat hate speech, incitement, defamatory content, or views that contradict established facts.
policy_text: Producing balanced coverage does not oblige us to give equal space to all sides of an issue. We do not have to repeat hate speech, defamatory comments and incitements to violence or propaganda. Nor are we required to quote views that contradict established facts when giving background information.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Access and Embedding vs. Editorial Independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept embedding terms, political campaign travel, or other access arrangements to obtain coverage, even if this structurally compromises independence.
pole_b: Maintain full editorial independence; guard against partisanship; pay your own way; treat all information from those providing access with appropriate scepticism.
policy_text: Embedded reporters are working in a military environment. They should treat all information from commanding officers and troops accordingly and guard against partisanship. It must be stated clearly in their text, photo or video production that the material was gathered while the journalist was embedded with the military. / If we travel with a political campaign we must pay our own way and not accept hospitality.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Publishing Graphic Content vs. Minimising Harm and Protecting Dignity
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Publish graphic images and videos because audiences have a right to see the full reality of atrocities, executions, injuries, and human suffering.
pole_b: Exercise rigorous editorial scrutiny before publishing graphic content; ask whether it adds to understanding in an essential way or only appeals to morbid interest; protect dignity; avoid giving perpetrators a propaganda platform.
policy_text: Careful consideration must be given to the publication of a graphic image or video. Editors must ask if it adds to the understanding of the story in an essential way, or only appeals to morbid interest. / Our policy is to release only a small number of still images taken from these videos that can enable the victim to be identified, and also to show the executioner, but under no circumstances should we show the moment of execution or the aftermath.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: No-Pay-Sources Rule vs. Paying for Newsworthy Eyewitness / UGC Content
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Pay sources, including eyewitnesses, for information and content of news value, using financial incentives to secure material that would otherwise be unavailable.
pole_b: Never pay sources for information; financial relationships corrupt journalistic independence and create incentives for fabrication.
policy_text: AFP journalists do not use information they have gathered for their personal benefit or use their position for financial gain. They do not pay sources. [entry #10] — but the UGC section states AFP will pay for authentic eyewitness content (implied by the verification and sourcing framework in Section 7 and confirmed in the extraction notes for entry #10).

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Withholding Kidnapping / Hostage News vs. Public's Right to Know
shared_tension_label: Public's right to information in crises vs. emergency/safety priority
pole_a: Report kidnappings and hostage situations as they occur; the public has a right to know, and AFP's role is to inform, not to withhold.
pole_b: Respect requests to withhold news of kidnappings when there are legitimate security reasons; the safety of hostages is paramount and overrides the default transparency obligation.
policy_text: The safety of hostages is paramount. AFP generally respects requests to withhold news of kidnappings if there are legitimate security reasons.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Personal Expression and External Activities vs. AFP Institutional Impartiality
shared_tension_label: Journalist's personal civic / political expression vs. professional neutrality
pole_a: Journalists retain full rights as private citizens to express personal views, engage in public life, and use social media freely, regardless of professional affiliation.
pole_b: Nothing a journalist does in their personal or public life should cast doubt on AFP's impartiality; personal expression, social media activity, and external activities must be clearly separated from AFP's professional capacity and must not impinge on AFP's reputation.
policy_text: While the Agency respects staff members' freedom to do so, there must be a clear separation between what is done in a personal capacity and in a professional capacity… the Agency's name should not be used for promotion or in campaigning. / AFP journalists identified as such on a social network must respect the Agency's values of impartiality and fairness and add a disclaimer in their profile that any opinions expressed are their own.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Embargo Compliance vs. Competitive Pressure to Publish
shared_tension_label: Embargo Compliance vs. Competitive Pressure to Publish
pole_a: Break embargoes when competitive pressure is intense, especially when there is reason to believe the information will soon be public anyway.
pole_b: Once an embargo is agreed, it creates an ethical obligation to hold; breaking it unilaterally (other than in defined exception circumstances) violates that obligation.
policy_text: Once we agree to handle a story with an embargo we are ethically obliged to respect it. However, that obligation ends the moment another news outlet breaks the embargo, or if they publish elements under an 'exclusive' tag with the tacit approval of the embargoed material's authors.

source_name: AFP Editorial Standards and Best Practices
tension_name: Conflict Coverage Access vs. Journalist Safety
shared_tension_label: Journalistic imperative vs. personal safety
pole_a: Send journalists into dangerous conflict zones regardless of risk, because the public's right to information from those areas justifies accepting danger as part of the job.
pole_b: Journalist safety is the overriding priority in conflict coverage; journalists have the right to refuse dangerous assignments; AFP will not accept production from freelancers in zones it considers too dangerous for its own staff.
policy_text: The most important thing in conflict reporting is the safety of our journalists and those who work with them. This must be the overriding factor when planning coverage. / Journalists have the right, without prejudice, to refuse a mission they consider too dangerous.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Legal compliance vs. public-interest journalism
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Breach or circumvent legal obligations when doing so is necessary to report on matters of significant public interest (e.g., handling leaked documents, trespass to obtain evidence, using data obtained unlawfully).
pole_b: Comply fully with all current and future relevant legislation and commit no illegal acts of any sort in the course of professional work, without exception.
policy_text: Members are obliged to be aware of their legal obligations and to ensure that they and their employees comply fully with these obligations and all future relevant legislation. / Members must obey the law in the pursuit of their duty. They must not commit illegal acts of any sort.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Confidentiality vs. transparency / public interest
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Disclose or use confidential information gathered in the course of business when doing so would serve the public interest or is required for honest, straightforward conduct with clients or the public.
pole_b: Keep confidential any information gathered in the course of business; use or disclose it only as required by statute, and maintain that duty even after the professional relationship ends.
policy_text: A duty of confidentiality exists in respect of information gathered in the course of business. Confidential information may only be used or disclosed in accordance with statutory requirements. The duty of confidentiality shall remain even after the relationship has been terminated.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Client loyalty vs. wider public interest
shared_tension_label: The public-interest test: genuine public interest vs. curiosity and proportionality
pole_a: Prioritise the client's interests fully, providing the best possible advice and service regardless of the effect on the wider public.
pole_b: Do the best for the client, but only within the outer boundary set by the wider public interest; where client interest and public interest conflict, public interest prevails.
policy_text: For our members this means doing the best for your client, but in doing so recognizing and respecting the wider public interest. / Always ensure that your client, or others to whom you have a professional responsibility, receive the best possible advice, support of performance of terms of engagement you have agreed to.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Independence and objectivity vs. conflicts of interest / third-party inducements
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept or retain gifts, hospitality, or other inducements from third parties, and manage personal or business interests privately without formal disclosure, on the basis that professional judgment is not in practice affected.
pole_b: Act objectively and free of any conflict of interest at all times; disclose actual or potential conflicts in writing as soon as practicable; immediately inform clients of any inducement offered by a third party; cease to act if the affected party does not give written consent to continuance.
policy_text: Members should at all times act objectively with honesty, free of any conflict of interest and not allow their actions or advice to be unduly influenced by others. / Where a member identifies the existence of, or the potential for, a conflict of interest he should, as soon as practicable, inform the person for whom he is acting, in writing, of the circumstances and unless such a person(s) consent(s) or request in writing to his continuing act, he must cease to act in provision of the service. / Where a member is offered any form of inducement by a third party or potential third party he shall immediately inform his client.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Mandatory error correction vs. reputational self-protection
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Minimise, delay, or quietly suppress corrections — particularly for small errors — to protect the professional reputation of the member, their firm, or the association.
pole_b: Correct errors — regardless of size — as soon as they are identified, with no exception for reputational concern.
policy_text: It is the policy of members to correct errors, large or small as soon as they become aware of them.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Accuracy and originality vs. deadline / competitive pressure
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Under deadline or competitive pressure, reproduce others' work without attribution (plagiarise) or publish information whose accuracy has not been verified (knowingly or recklessly false information).
pole_b: Always produce original work with proper attribution and publish only information that is truthful and accurate; knowingly or recklessly providing false information or plagiarising constitutes a betrayal of the association.
policy_text: Members who plagiarize or knowingly or recklessly provide false information for publication shall betray our Association.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Professional conduct standards extended to private life vs. personal autonomy
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: Professional ethics obligations apply only to conduct in the course of professional work; members' private behaviour is their own affair and should not be subject to professional-code scrutiny.
pole_b: Members must act in a manner consistent with professional and positive values in both their professional AND private life, and must be aware that individual conduct — including in private — can bring the entire association into disrepute.
policy_text: Act in a manner, both in your professional and private life, to promote you, your firm, or the organization you work for, in a professional and positive way. / The behavior of a single member can bring the whole Association into disrepute.

source_name: AIPS Code of Professional Conduct Standards
tension_name: Obligation to raise concerns about colleagues vs. professional solidarity
shared_tension_label: Professional solidarity vs. accountability for unethical colleagues
pole_a: Stay silent about a colleague's apparent misconduct (conflict of interest, acceptance of gifts or hospitality, inappropriate behaviour) out of professional loyalty or to avoid damaging collegial relationships.
pole_b: Raise concerns promptly when professional standards appear not to be met, including specifically in relation to conflict of interest, gifts, and hospitality.
policy_text: These include conflict of interest, gifts, hospitality, and raising concerns when it appears standards are not being met or when there is inappropriate behavior.

source_name: Al Jazeera Code of Ethics
tension_name: Truth-telling vs. Balance / False equivalence
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Present multiple perspectives with equal weight to satisfy the value of balance, even when evidence clearly favours one position over others.
pole_b: Declare the truth unequivocally and in a manner that leaves no doubt about its validity and accuracy, even if doing so disadvantages one side of a debate.
policy_text: Endeavour to get to the truth and declare it in our dispatches, programmes and news bulletins unequivocally in a manner which leaves no doubt about its validity and accuracy. / Adhere to the journalistic values of honesty, courage, fairness, balance, independence, credibility and diversity… / Present the diverse points of view and opinions without bias and partiality.

source_name: Al Jazeera Code of Ethics
tension_name: Speed and competitive pressure vs. Editorial standards
shared_tension_label: Online publishing speed and openness vs. pre-publication editorial control
pole_a: Prioritise breaking a story first — ahead of rivals — even if doing so means publishing before accuracy, fairness, or other editorial standards can be fully met.
pole_b: Welcome fair competition but never allow the goal of getting a scoop to become an end in itself; maintain editorial standards regardless of competitive pressure.
policy_text: Welcome fair and honest media competition without allowing it to affect adversely our standards of performance and thereby having a 'scoop' would not become an end in itself.

source_name: Al Jazeera Code of Ethics
tension_name: Editorial independence vs. Institutional and political entanglement
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow the outlet's institutional relationships — including state funding, cooperative ties with regional journalistic unions, and political affiliations — to shape editorial decisions.
pole_b: Give professional journalistic considerations absolute priority over commercial and political considerations in all editorial decisions, regardless of the outlet's institutional context.
policy_text: giving no priority to commercial or political over professional consideration. / Cooperate with Arab and international journalistic unions and associations to defend freedom of the press.

source_name: Al Jazeera Code of Ethics
tension_name: Acknowledging errors vs. Credibility and competitive standing
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Delay, minimise, or avoid publicly acknowledging errors to protect the outlet's credibility and avoid handing competitive advantage to rivals.
pole_b: Acknowledge mistakes promptly and publicly when they occur, correct them fully, and take active steps to prevent recurrence — even at short-term reputational cost.
policy_text: Acknowledge a mistake when it occurs, promptly correct it and ensure it does not recur.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Source protection vs. public interest disclosure
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Always protect a confidential source's identity, regardless of what the source has done or what harm may result.
pole_b: Protect the identity of confidential sources as the binding default; break anonymity only in the three narrowly defined circumstances stated in the code.
policy_text: Journalists shall not divulge the name of a person when information is provided on a confidential basis, unless consent has been explicitly given by the person concerned.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Transparency of methods vs. investigative effectiveness
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever methods — including covert or deceptive ones — are most effective for gathering information, without necessarily disclosing them.
pole_b: Use transparent and lawful methods as the default; resort to subterfuge, hidden recording equipment, or concealment of professional identity only when both conditions are met: no other means is available and the matter is of urgent and serious public concern. Disclose covert methods used, in the story or when circumstances permit.
policy_text: Journalists will use fair methods in the collection of information. They only make use of subterfuge, hidden cameras, microphones or other special equipment, or obscure their professional identity, in circumstances where: a) There is no other means to obtain the information concerned b) The information is of urgent and serious concern to the public. / Journalists shall indicate when such methods have been used in the story or provide disclosure when circumstances permit.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Privacy vs. accountability
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish information about individuals' private lives when it interests the public or advances the story, without requiring a specific public-interest justification.
pole_b: Respect every individual's right to privacy; restrict journalistic intrusion into private life to cases where genuine public interest — as narrowly defined in §17 — justifies it. Apply a higher but not unlimited privacy entitlement to private individuals; accept that public figures have reduced (but non-zero) privacy expectations.
policy_text: A journalist must respect the right of an individual to privacy. Only the protection of the public interest can justify journalistic investigations which interfere with the private aspects of the lives of individuals. / Public figures are entitled to less privacy than other individuals. However, information on their private lives and information related to their family and friends should be disclosed only when it serves the public interest.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Right to publish vs. right of reply and fairness
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish on deadline or publish first, without always waiting to contact all affected parties or incorporating their responses.
pole_b: Ensure all parties in a controversy have the opportunity to state their position before publication; guarantee criticised parties the right to respond, where possible in the same publication; go beyond mere contact attempts to genuinely present all sides.
policy_text: In reporting on a controversy, journalists should be inclusive and seek to ensure that all parties concerned have an opportunity to state their position. / Criticized parties shall have the right to respond to accusations, whenever possible in the same publication. / Mere contacts with both sides do not 'release' a journalist from the obligation to present both sides of a story, and to report as truthfully as possible.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Accuracy and correction vs. editorial reputation
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Minimise, delay, or bury corrections to protect the outlet's credibility and avoid embarrassment.
pole_b: When inaccuracy or misleading content can be demonstrated, publish a clear and appropriately prominent correction; provide an apology and appropriate remedy where necessary; engage openly with audience complaints.
policy_text: Media should publish a clear and appropriately prominent correction when it can be demonstrated that inaccurate or misleading information has been published. Media should provide an apology and appropriate remedy where it is necessary.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Full reporting of violence and crime vs. avoiding harm and sensationalism
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report violence, crime, and disasters in full graphic detail to convey the true scale and severity of events, maximising impact and audience engagement.
pole_b: Report violence, crime, and disasters with care, restraint, and sensitivity: do not sensationalise; respect the dignity of victims and their families; protect minors and vulnerable groups; do not glorify crime or terrorism; withhold explicit imagery that would insult relatives or the public.
policy_text: Violence and brutality shall not be sensationalized. Reporting must take due account of the need to protect minors and vulnerable groups in society. / Media shall not sensationalize reporting with explicit pictures of catastrophes, accidents or violence that might insult the feelings of the relatives as well as sensibilities of the public. / Journalists shall respect the dignity of victims and their families and shall allow people to grieve in private and will report such matters with sympathy and constraint.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Presumption of innocence vs. accountability journalism
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report credible evidence of wrongdoing as conclusive; describe suspects and charged individuals as criminals to convey the seriousness of the allegations.
pole_b: Always respect the presumption of innocence; never describe someone as a criminal before final court conviction; report court proceedings accurately, fairly, and without prejudice to the right to a fair trial.
policy_text: Journalists will always respect presumption of innocence and will refrain from describing someone as a criminal prior to final court conviction. / Reporting from the courthouse (including the publishing and broadcasting of images), should be accurate, fair, not prejudicial, and fully respectful of the right to a fair trial.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Child protection vs. public right to know
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Report on events involving children in the same way as events involving adults, because the public has an equal right to information about crime, abuse, or danger affecting minors.
pole_b: Apply heightened protection to children and people with limited abilities: do not interview under-18s on personal issues without a parent or responsible adult present; do not publish images or information about a child's private life without overriding public interest; do not exploit children's innocence or trust; obtain proper authorisation before publishing photographs and names of missing young persons.
policy_text: Journalists shall not take advantage of children's innocence and trust and will publish information or images about the private life of a child only if there is an overriding public interest. / Journalists shall not normally interview children under 18 on personal issues in the absence of parents or responsible persons.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Identification of group identity vs. non-discrimination
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Routinely specify the ethnicity, religion, nationality, race, or sexual orientation of individuals and groups as contextual detail in reporting, regardless of whether this information is necessary to understand the story.
pole_b: Refrain from specifying group identity characteristics unless they are deemed relevant and necessary to understanding the facts and opinions in the publication; actively oppose discrimination in media content; do not publish material that incites hatred or violence based on identity characteristics.
policy_text: Any publication should refrain from specifying the origin, ethnicity, nationality, race, religion or sexual orientation of a group or an individual, unless it is deemed relevant and necessary to better understand facts and opinions presented in the publication. / Media must not publish materials that incites intense hatred or violence towards individuals based on race, religion, nationality, color, ethnic origin, membership, gender, sexual orientation, civil status, disability, illness or age.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Public interest vs. public curiosity
shared_tension_label: The public-interest test: genuine public interest vs. curiosity and proportionality
pole_a: Treat "what audiences want to know about" as sufficient justification for departing from code protections on privacy, dignity, source confidentiality, and accuracy.
pole_b: Distinguish rigorously between genuine public interest — defined as urgent health/safety concerns, finding or preventing serious crime and abuse of power, and protecting the public from serious deception — and what is merely interesting to the public. Only genuine public interest can justify departing from code provisions.
policy_text: The terms of this Code provide essential and necessary guidelines for the exercise of ethical journalism and may only be disregarded in exceptional circumstances in order to serve the public interest. / Legitimate public interest does not justify sensationalism and in the spirit of this Code it should never be confused with information that is 'interesting to the public'.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Rescue operations vs. right to be informed
shared_tension_label: Public's right to information in crises vs. emergency/safety priority
pole_a: The public's right to real-time information about accidents and disasters is paramount; journalists should cover events as they unfold without deferring to emergency responders.
pole_b: In accidents and disasters, rescue operations take precedence over the public's right to be informed; journalistic coverage must not impede or interfere with rescue efforts.
policy_text: In the case of accidents and disasters, media shall bear in mind that rescue operations for victims and persons in jeopardy take precedence over the public's right to be informed.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Editorial autonomy over reader comments vs. openness and prior commitments
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish all reader comments and letters without pre-screening or post-publication removal, treating open comment sections as an expression of freedom of expression.
pole_b: Establish and publish clear terms and conditions for comments; monitor and enforce them; investigate serious accusations in reader content before publishing; remove abusive, hateful, or malicious content after publication; but honour prior publication commitments and preserve essential meaning when editing.
policy_text: Media and editorial staff should agree to and publish clearly defined terms and conditions for the selection and publishing of comments from the public. Media shall monitor and review such comments and take steps to ensure the terms and conditions of publication are respected. / the editorial staff, or the editors, may delete or remove unacceptable comments from publication where it is abusive, hateful, or is found to contain malicious and unfounded allegations.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Confidentiality of workplace information vs. whistle-blowing duty
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Maintain confidentiality about internal newsroom matters in all circumstances, protecting colleagues, employers, and workplace culture from external exposure.
pole_b: Respect the confidentiality of workplace information as the default; but do not maintain confidentiality where the information relates to violations of laws or the Code of Ethics — in those cases, the code's own enforcement mechanisms and legal obligations take precedence.
policy_text: Journalists shall respect the confidentiality of their workplace where this information is not related to violations of laws and the Code of Ethics.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Embargo compliance vs. competitive pressure
shared_tension_label: Embargo Compliance vs. Competitive Pressure to Publish
pole_a: Break an agreed embargo when a competitor publishes the embargoed information first, on the grounds that the information is already public.
pole_b: Respect pre-publication embargo agreements and do not publish embargoed information before the agreed time, unless the embargo is voided by another party's breach or the embargo-setter's own violation of the agreement's terms.
policy_text: Journalists who agree not to publish a piece of information or material for a given period of time must respect these arrangements. Such an agreement (embargo) should be considered null and void if the information is published by another party, or when the person who requested the embargo in any way violates terms and conditions of the agreement reached between parties.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Pre-publication review vs. editorial independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial independence vs. Subject approval rights
pole_a: Allow sources or interested parties to review and effectively control content before publication, treating their approval as a condition of the story running.
pole_b: Offer pre-publication review to interested parties in the interests of fairness and accuracy, but retain full editorial independence: no party has a veto on publication, and the journalist remains free to decide which suggestions to adopt.
policy_text: In the interests of fairness and accuracy journalists may show their news stories to interested parties prior to publication, but they shall not grant a veto on the right to publish and shall be free to decide for themselves on what suggestions they should take under consideration.

source_name: Albania Code of Ethics for Journalists
tension_name: Fair competition vs. professional solidarity
shared_tension_label: Fair competition vs. professional solidarity
pole_a: Pursue competitive advantage aggressively: publish first, protect exclusive information, undercut rivals, and use any legal means to outperform competitors.
pole_b: Maintain appropriate balance between fair competition and professional solidarity; do not impede colleagues in gathering information, mislead them, or report them to authorities; do not use mass media for personal or professional rivalries; respect colleagues' right to work.
policy_text: In their business relations media and journalists should recognize the importance of fair competition and professional solidarity and maintain appropriate balance between the two. / The journalist should not impede the colleagues to gather information, to mislead them intentionally, or report on them to the authorities.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Speed vs. accuracy in breaking news
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly to meet competitive deadlines, even if verification is incomplete.
pole_b: Hold the story until all reasonable verification steps — multiple sources, factual confirmation, subject response — are complete, regardless of competitive pressure.
policy_text: The AP routinely seeks and requires more than one source. Stories should be held while attempts are made to reach additional sources for confirmation or elaboration. / They have gone to great lengths… to ensure that the news was reported quickly, accurately and honestly.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Source transparency vs. source protection
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Grant anonymity readily to obtain information, prioritising the story over readers' ability to evaluate source credibility.
pole_b: Identify all sources by name; grant anonymity only when all of a strict multi-condition test is satisfied, the source's identity is known to a manager, the reason for anonymity is disclosed in the story, and descriptive attribution is provided to establish credibility.
policy_text: Transparency is critical to our credibility with the public and our subscribers. Whenever possible, we pursue information on the record. / It means we always strive to identify all the sources of our information, shielding them with anonymity only when they insist upon it and when they provide vital information – not opinion or speculation; when there is no other way to obtain that information; and when we know the source is knowledgeable and reliable.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Verbatim accuracy vs. editorial clarity in quotations
shared_tension_label: Verbatim Accuracy of Quotes vs. Editorial Responsibility for Harmful / Clumsy Language
pole_a: Clean up quotations for grammar, clarity, or concision to make the story more readable, even if this slightly alters the speaker's words.
pole_b: Reproduce quotations exactly as spoken; if a quotation is grammatically flawed or unclear, paraphrase it in a way completely true to the original meaning rather than altering the quoted words.
policy_text: Quotations must be accurate, and precise. / We do not alter quotations, even to correct grammatical errors or word usage. / If a quotation is flawed because of grammar or lack of clarity, the writer must paraphrase in a way that is completely true to the original meaning.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Photographic/audio/video truth vs. permissible technical improvement
shared_tension_label: Accuracy and transparency in visual presentation vs. editorial/creative presentation needs
pole_a: Apply whatever technical processing best serves visual or audio quality, clarity, or aesthetic standards, even if this alters the original captured content.
pole_b: Preserve the truthful content of images and recordings exactly as captured; permit only the narrowly defined set of technical adjustments that do not alter editorial meaning, and escalate any uncertainty to a senior editor before transmission.
policy_text: AP pictures must always tell the truth. We do not alter or digitally manipulate the content of a photograph in any way. / For video, the AP permits the use of subtle, standard methods of improving technical quality… provided the use of these methods does not conceal, obscure, remove or otherwise alter the content, or any portion of the content, of the image. / AP's audio actualities must always tell the truth. We do not alter or manipulate the content of a newsmaker actuality in any way.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Individual civic/political freedom vs. institutional independence
shared_tension_label: Journalist's personal civic / political expression vs. professional neutrality
pole_a: Journalists retain full democratic rights of political participation, public expression, and civic engagement as private citizens.
pole_b: AP journalists — especially editorial employees — must subordinate personal political activity and public opinion expression to the organisation's need to appear and be unbiased, regardless of whether the journalist covers politics.
policy_text: Anyone who works for the AP must be mindful that opinions they express may damage the AP's reputation as an unbiased source of news. They must refrain from declaring their views on contentious public issues in any public forum… and must not take part in demonstrations in support of causes or movements. / Editorial employees are expected to be scrupulous in avoiding any political activity, whether they cover politics regularly or not.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Fairness to subjects vs. publication timeliness
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish a negative story promptly without waiting for a response, particularly when competitive pressures or story urgency are high.
pole_b: Make significant efforts to reach any person portrayed negatively, give them a reasonable amount of time to respond, and explain in the story what contact efforts were made if they could not be reached.
policy_text: Whenever we portray someone in a negative light, we must make a real effort to obtain a response from that person. / We must make significant efforts to reach anyone who may be portrayed in a negative way in our stories, and we must give them a reasonable amount of time to get back to us before we move the story.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Public interest disclosure vs. protection of vulnerable individuals
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Publish all factually accurate information relevant to a story, including identities of victims and accused, in the interest of full public transparency.
pole_b: Withhold the identities of sexual assault victims, pre-teenage children accused of or witnessing crimes, and others whose identification serves no public interest commensurate with the harm to the individual.
policy_text: We do not generally identify those who say they have been sexually assaulted or pre-teenage children who are accused of crimes or who are witnesses to them, except in unusual circumstances.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Corrections transparency vs. institutional reputation management
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Minimise the visibility and labelling of errors through euphemistic language ("clarification," "update," "recast") to protect AP's reputation and avoid drawing attention to mistakes.
pole_b: Correct errors fully, quickly, and ungrudgingly; label every factual correction as a "correction" without euphemism; ensure correctives reach every outlet that used the erroneous information.
policy_text: When mistakes are made, they must be corrected – fully, quickly and ungrudgingly. / A correction must always be labeled a correction in the editor's note. We do not use euphemisms such as 'recasts,' 'fixes,' 'clarifies' or 'changes' when correcting a factual error.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Avoiding financial conflicts vs. personal financial autonomy
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Journalists retain full autonomy over their personal financial decisions, including investment portfolios, regardless of their reporting beat.
pole_b: Business/financial journalists must divest all holdings in companies they cover; editors and writers covering financial markets may not own individual equities at all; all employees must avoid speculative trading activity; household members' financial interests must also be monitored and disclosed.
policy_text: These employees must not own stock, equities or have any personal financial investment or involvement with any company, enterprise or industry that they regularly cover for the AP. / Financial news employees must also avoid investment activities that are speculative or driven by day-trading or short-term profit goals because such activities may create the impression that the employee is seeking to drive market factors or is acting upon information that is not available to the public.

source_name: AP News Values and Principles
tension_name: Access to news events and sources vs. editorial independence
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept subsidised travel, free tickets, gifts, honorary positions, or payment from newsmakers when necessary to maintain access to important news events or sources.
pole_b: Pay AP's own way for travel and event access; refuse gifts above nominal value; decline payment from newsmakers; decline honoraria from organisations with conflicts of interest; refuse free tickets except for coverage purposes; and push back against background briefings even at the risk of reduced access.
policy_text: It means we don't pay newsmakers for interviews, to take their photographs or to film or record them. / If a trip is organized, and we think the trip is newsworthy, we go and pay our way. / We do not accept free tickets to sports, entertainment or other events for anything other than coverage purposes. / AP reporters should object vigorously when a source wants to brief a group of reporters on background and try to persuade the source to put the briefing on the record.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Financial independence vs. operational access to coverage infrastructure
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept free or subsidised travel, lodging, food, services (phone, fax, typewriter) and event access from the teams and leagues being covered, on the grounds that full reimbursement is operationally impractical.
pole_b: The newspaper pays every staffer's travel, accommodation, food, and drink; reimburses teams for any services provided; and, when a direct bill is impossible, estimates and pays the commercial-airline-equivalent cost — so that no financial dependency on covered parties exists.
policy_text: The newspaper pays its staffer's way for travel, accommodations, food and drink. / If a staffer travels on a chartered team plane, the newspaper should insist on being billed. If the team cannot issue a bill, the amount can be calculated by estimating the cost of a similar flight on a commercial airline. / When services are provided to a newspaper by a pro or college team, those teams should be reimbursed by the newspaper.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Absolute no-gift rule vs. pragmatic tolerance of trivial or publicly available benefits
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept any gift, deal, or discount offered, including those of non-trivial value, on the grounds that personal relationships and hospitality are normal parts of beat journalism.
pole_b: Refuse all gifts, deals, and discounts; if a gift is impossible to return, donate it to charity rather than keep it; accept only items of genuinely insignificant value or those available identically to the general public.
policy_text: No deals, discounts or gifts except those of insignificant value or those available to the public. / If a gift is impossible or impractical to return, donate a gift to charity. / Do not accept free memberships or reduced fees for memberships. Do not accept gratis use of facilities, such as golf courses or tennis courts, unless it is used as part of doing a story for the newspaper.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Conflict-of-interest avoidance vs. journalists' personal autonomy and supplemental income
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Allow journalists to pursue outside employment, media appearances, and community roles freely as a matter of personal and financial autonomy, leaving conflict-of-interest judgments to the individual.
pole_b: Editors and reporters must avoid outside activities or employment — including writing for team publications, serving as official scorers, and prioritising broadcast appearances over newspaper obligations — that create or even appear to create a conflict of interest.
policy_text: Editors and reporters should avoid taking part in outside activities or employment that might create conflict of interest or even appearance of a conflict. / They should not serve as an official scorer at baseball games. / They should not write for team or league media guides or other team or league publications. This has the potential of compromising a reporter's disinterested observations. / Staffers who appear on radio or television should understand that their first loyalty is to the paper.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Individual firsthand reporting vs. collective note and quote pooling
shared_tension_label: Verbatim Accuracy of Quotes vs. Editorial Responsibility for Harmful / Clumsy Language
pole_a: Pool and share notes and quotes freely among reporters as a standard practice of sports coverage, especially at press conferences and in restricted-access environments.
pole_b: Discourage note and quote pooling; when secondhand quotes must be used, disclose their origin to readers by attributing the quote to the source newspaper or reporter.
policy_text: Sharing and pooling of notes and quotes should be discouraged. / If a reporter uses quotes gained secondhand, that should be made known to the readers. A quote could be attributed to a newspaper or to another reporter.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Participation in the sports ecosystem vs. editorial impartiality
shared_tension_label: Participation in the sports ecosystem vs. editorial impartiality
pole_a: Participate fully in awards voting, all-star selections, and other quasi-official sports functions on the grounds that journalistic participation adds credibility and maintains source relationships within the sport.
pole_b: Carefully evaluate whether participation in awards voting or all-star selection creates a conflict of interest; where it does, decline to participate.
policy_text: A newspaper should carefully consider the implications of voting for all awards and all-star teams and decide if such voting creates a conflict of interest.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: Apply rules mechanically, treating the written guidelines as exhaustive and sufficient to resolve every ethical situation without the exercise of individual judgment.
pole_b: Treat the written guidelines as a framework, not an exhaustive rulebook; use common sense and good professional judgment to fill gaps and adapt the code to local conditions.
policy_text: Guidelines can't cover everything. Use common sense and good judgment in applying these guidelines in adopting local codes.

source_name: APSE Ethics Guidelines (Associated Press Sports Editors)
tension_name: Merit-only assignments vs. identity-conscious diversity practices
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Make assignment decisions with reference to the race or gender of reporters, whether to promote diversity in bylines and coverage or to match reporter identity to community identity.
pole_b: Make all assignment decisions solely on merit, without regard to race or gender.
policy_text: Assignments should be made on merit, without regard for race or gender.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Transparent self-identification vs. undercover/investigative newsgathering
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Conceal journalist identity to gather information that subjects would not provide if they knew they were speaking to press — particularly in investigations of powerful actors who would otherwise obstruct reporting.
pole_b: Always identify yourself openly as a media representative when gathering news, photographs, or documents, using only fair, open, and honest means throughout the newsgathering process.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall resort only to fair, open and honest means or efforts to obtain news, photographs or documents necessary to enable him/her to carry out his/her professional work, properly identifying him/herself in the process as being a representative from media.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Full honest reporting vs. protection of national security and regional stability
shared_tension_label: Honest reporting on armed conflict vs. rejection of war propaganda
pole_a: Publish truthful, complete reporting on government conduct, military activity, cross-border disputes, or sensitive security matters even when the reporting may embarrass states, inflame diplomatic tensions, or be characterised by authorities as a threat to national security.
pole_b: Report honestly and accurately, but refrain from writing reports, opinions, or comments that would endanger the security of one's country or foment armed confrontation between ASEAN member states; actively promote closer friendly relations among them.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall not write reports, opinions or comments which would endanger the security of his/her country or foment armed confrontation between his/her country and any other ASEAN country, striving at all times, instead, to promote closer friendly relations among them. / The ASEAN journalist shall honestly report and interpret the news, making sure to the best of his/her knowledge and ability, not to suppress essential facts or distort the truth through exaggeration or through wrong or improper emphasis.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Truthful reporting vs. protection of private persons' reputation
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Publish truthful, fully accurate information about a private person even when doing so will damage or destroy their honour or reputation, on the grounds that accuracy is the primary journalistic obligation.
pole_b: Refrain from publishing reports that destroy a private person's honour or reputation, unless the public interest is sufficient to justify it; treat reputation protection as a genuine editorial constraint, not merely a legal one.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall refrain from writing reports which have the effect of destroying the honour or reputation of a private person, unless public interest justifies it.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. verifiability and the public's right to know
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Identify sources or disclose confidential information when doing so would allow the public to better evaluate the credibility of a report, when a subject aggrieved by the report needs the information to respond, or when external pressure (legal or governmental) compels disclosure.
pole_b: Never identify a source who has specifically requested confidentiality; resist all outside attempts to compel disclosure; treat confidential information obtained in the course of journalistic work as inviolable.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall not identify his/her source, and shall resist any outside attempt to make him/her do so, when specifically so enjoined by his/her informant. / The ASEAN journalist shall not violate confidential information or material obtained by him/her in the exercise of his/her calling.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Right of reply vs. journalistic accuracy
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Decline to publish a right-of-reply response — or publish it with strong editorial qualification — when the journalist believes the reply contains material falsehoods that would mislead readers and undermine the accuracy of the original report.
pole_b: Give any person aggrieved by a report or interpretation of news the right to reply, treating fairness to the subject as a procedural obligation independent of the journalist's assessment of the reply's truth.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall give any person aggrieved by his/her report or interpretation of the news the right of reply.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Respect for ethnic/cultural/religious diversity vs. honest reporting on social tensions
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Report fully and accurately on ethnic, cultural, or religious tensions, conflicts, or harms — including quoting inflammatory statements by real actors — even when the reporting may be perceived as disrespecting or destabilising the diverse fabric of ASEAN societies.
pole_b: Pay due regard to the multi-ethnic, cultural, and religious fabric of ASEAN countries in all reporting, treating this as an active editorial constraint on how stories about communal differences are framed and presented.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall pay due regard to the multi-ethnic, cultural and religious fabric of ASEAN countries.

source_name: ASEAN Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Independence from personal and financial interests vs. editorial autonomy
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Exercise editorial discretion in ways that inevitably reflect the journalist's personal values, cultural background, or commercial relationships — acknowledging that complete neutrality is an unachievable standard — and prioritise the story's public-interest value over strict financial independence.
pole_b: Refuse any payment, gift, or other consideration in exchange for false reporting or suppression of truth; keep personal motives and interests entirely separate from reporting so that professional integrity and the dignity of the profession are not compromised.
policy_text: The ASEAN journalist shall not allow personal motives or interests to influence him/her or to colour his/her views in a manner that would reflect on his/her professional integrity or would undermine the dignity of his/her profession. / The ASEAN journalist shall not demand or accept any payment, gift or other consideration by way of recompense for reporting what is not true, or withholding or suppressing the truth.

source_name: Asian Federation of Environmental Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Human-rights framing of the environment vs. independence from all vested interests
shared_tension_label: Advocacy journalism vs. objectivity and neutrality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Treat environmental stories as empirical, contested matters of fact and policy, without presupposing a rights framework that could itself be read as an ideological or political position.
pole_b: Frame environmental reporting within the understanding that a clean environment is a fundamental right linked to life, health, and well-being, so that human rights dimensions are always surfaced.
policy_text: The right to a clean environment and sustainable development is fundamental and is closely connected to the right to life and good health and well being… The journalists should not be influenced on these issues by vested interests – whether they are commercial, political, and government or non-governmental.

source_name: Asian Federation of Environmental Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Early public warning vs. verification before publication
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish an alert about an environmental threat as soon as a credible indication exists, prioritising the public's need for early warning over the time-consuming process of full source verification.
pole_b: Cross-check the authenticity of every source — commercial, official, or non-governmental — before relying on it, and avoid alarmist or speculative reportage, even when urgency pressures suggest early publication.
policy_text: The journalist should as far as possible cite sources of information and avoid alarmist or speculative reportage and tendentious comment… He or she should crosscheck the authenticity of a source, whether commercial, official or non-governmental.

source_name: Asian Federation of Environmental Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Informing the public about disaster vs. respecting victims' privacy
shared_tension_label: Public's right to information in crises vs. emergency/safety priority
pole_a: Prioritise the public's right to full and vivid information about environmental catastrophes, even when doing so requires depicting, naming, or quoting individuals who have been harmed.
pole_b: Respect the privacy of individuals affected by environmental catastrophes and natural disasters, refraining from intrusive coverage of their personal circumstances even in the course of legitimate environmental reporting.
policy_text: The journalist should respect the right of privacy of individuals who have been affected by environmental catastrophes, natural disasters and the like.

source_name: Asian Federation of Environmental Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Correcting the record and shifting public opinion vs. avoiding tendentious comment
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Maintain the original framing of a story once published; avoid actions that could be perceived as deliberately "tilting" public opinion, in keeping with the prohibition on tendentious comment.
pole_b: Correct previously published errors without hesitation and revise analysis in light of subsequent developments, even when this deliberately shifts the balance of public opinion — accepting that intellectual honesty requires updating the record regardless of the effect on opinion.
policy_text: The environmental journalist should not hesitate to correct information that he or she previously believed was correct… or to tilt the balance of public opinion by analysis in the light of subsequent developments… avoid alarmist or speculative reportage and tendentious comment.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Independence vs. industry access
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept press trips, product samples, tastings, sponsored travel and lodging, and commercially sponsored contests because they are standard operating practice in food journalism and refusing them makes beat coverage operationally unworkable.
pole_b: Refuse all gifts, favours, free travel or lodging, special treatment, privileges, and commercially sponsored contests, regardless of industry norms, because acceptance compromises integrity and credibility.
policy_text: Gifts, favors, free travel or lodging, special treatment or privileges can compromise the integrity and diminish the credibility of food journalists, as well as that of their employers. This includes commercially sponsored contests. Such offers should be avoided.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Objectivity vs. opinion expression
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Allow journalists to express personal views, preferences, and evaluations freely throughout their work, reflecting the inherently subjective nature of food criticism and journalism.
pole_b: Report news as accurately and as objectively as possible, and when personal views are published, clearly label them as opinion so readers can distinguish them from factual news reporting.
policy_text: Report news objectively; when publishing personal views or editorials, label them clearly so they cannot be mistaken for factual news reports.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Editorial integrity vs. commercial pressure (brand naming)
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Name brands, companies, and interest groups freely throughout editorial coverage because food journalism is inherently product-specific and readers need precise brand information to make decisions.
pole_b: Restrict use of brand names and company names in editorial content to contexts that are genuinely newsworthy or necessary for clarification, so that editorial space is not converted into advertising.
policy_text: Because the editorial space allotted to food journalism is not an extension of advertising, brand names or names of specific companies or interest groups should be used only in a newsworthy context or for purposes of clarification.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Byline integrity vs. collaborative and aggregative practice
shared_tension_label: Verbatim Accuracy of Quotes vs. Editorial Responsibility for Harmful / Clumsy Language
pole_a: Allow bylines to reflect editorial brand, team authorship, or aggregation conventions rather than individual authorship, as is common in digital and collaborative newsroom workflows.
pole_b: Attach your byline only to material you yourself have written; credit all incorporated material to its actual source.
policy_text: Food journalists should use their bylines only in conjunction with material that they have written. Material from other sources incorporated in a story should be credited.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Verification vs. speed (press-release reliance)
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish or repeat information from press releases and news communications directly, relying on the issuing organisation's authority and the competitive pressure to be timely, without independent verification.
pole_b: Substantiate all so-called news communications and press releases before relying on them, to assure accuracy.
policy_text: To assure accuracy, so-called news communications or press releases should be substantiated.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Professional role vs. personal benefit (use of position)
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Leverage the access and relationships that come with a food journalist's role to obtain preferential treatment, reservations, discounts, exclusive access, or other personal benefits — treating this as a reasonable professional perk.
pole_b: Never use your journalistic position to win favours for yourself or for others; the role confers access for reporting purposes only.
policy_text: Similarly, food journalists should not use their positions to win favors for themselves or for others.

source_name: Association of Food Journalists Code of Ethics
tension_name: Civic participation vs. conflict of interest (secondary roles)
shared_tension_label: Journalist's personal civic / political expression vs. professional neutrality
pole_a: Participate fully in civic life, take on secondary employment, hold public office, and join organisations of interest to you, treating these affiliations as a journalist's right regardless of how they may be perceived.
pole_b: Avoid secondary employment, political involvement, public office, and organisational memberships that compromise your integrity as a food journalist.
policy_text: Secondary employment, political involvement, holding public office or serving in organizations should be avoided if it compromises the integrity of a food journalist.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Press freedom vs. public responsibility
shared_tension_label: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish facts and opinions freely, without constraint, treating press freedom as the paramount and essentially unlimited value.
pole_b: Exercise press freedom within the bounds of public responsibility; recognise that "liberty does not mean licence" and that other important freedoms, rights, and values must be given due regard.
policy_text: Freedom of the press, however, carries responsibilities to the public. Liberty does not mean licence, and due regard must be given to other important freedoms, rights and values which are in the public interest.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Speed / completeness of publication vs. accuracy
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish available information quickly — especially in breaking-news conditions — accepting that some factual material may later prove inaccurate or misleading.
pole_b: Ensure that factual material is accurate and not misleading before publication, regardless of competitive or timing pressure.
policy_text: Ensure that factual material in news reports and elsewhere is accurate and not misleading, and is distinguishable from other material such as opinion.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Accurate / truthful reporting vs. harm avoidance
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Publish accurate, complete factual information even when doing so causes substantial offence, distress, prejudice, or risk to health and safety.
pole_b: Avoid publishing material — even accurate material — that causes or materially contributes to substantial offence, distress, prejudice, or a substantial risk to health or safety, unless doing so is sufficiently in the public interest.
policy_text: Avoid causing or contributing materially to substantial offence, distress or prejudice, or a substantial risk to health or safety, unless doing so is sufficiently in the public interest.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Editorial opinion freedom vs. factual discipline
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Express opinions forcefully and selectivity, choosing which facts to cite in support of a view, without being constrained by a duty to present all key facts or to clearly label opinion as distinct from factual reporting.
pole_b: Clearly distinguish opinion from factual material, ensure opinion is not based on significantly inaccurate facts or omission of key facts, and present factual material with reasonable fairness and balance.
policy_text: Ensure that factual material is presented with reasonable fairness and balance, and that writers' expressions of opinion are not based on significantly inaccurate factual material or omission of key facts.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Privacy vs. public-interest accountability
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish information about a person's private life or affairs whenever it is newsworthy or the public is interested, without weighing the intrusion against a structured public-interest test.
pole_b: Respect a person's reasonable expectations of privacy; intrude only when doing so is sufficiently in the public interest, with the required justification calibrated to the gravity of the intrusion.
policy_text: Avoid intruding on a person's reasonable expectations of privacy, unless doing so is sufficiently in the public interest.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Investigative / undercover methods vs. integrity and transparency norms
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever newsgathering methods — including deception, subterfuge, or hidden recording — are necessary to expose wrongdoing and serve the public interest.
pole_b: Avoid publishing material gathered by deceptive or unfair means; where such means are used, ensure the public-interest justification is sufficient and proportionate to the gravity of the deception employed.
policy_text: Avoid publishing material which has been gathered by deceptive or unfair means, unless doing so is sufficiently in the public interest.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Editorial control vs. right of reply
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Treat editorial decisions about what to publish — including decisions not to publish responses — as entirely within the publisher's discretion, with no obligation to carry material it would not otherwise choose to run.
pole_b: Give a person a fair opportunity for subsequent publication of a reply when published material refers adversely to them and a reply is reasonably necessary to address a potential breach of the privacy/harm-avoidance principle.
policy_text: Ensure that where material refers adversely to a person, a fair opportunity is given for subsequent publication of a reply if that is reasonably necessary to address a possible breach of General Principle 3.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Bright-line rule certainty vs. proportionate case-by-case judgment
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: Apply fixed, categorical rules — the same public-interest threshold in every case — for predictability and consistency, regardless of how serious the potential breach is.
pole_b: Calibrate the required level of public-interest justification to the gravity of the potential breach; more serious intrusions, harms, or deceptions require stronger public-interest grounds before they are permissible.
policy_text: The necessary level of justification in the public interest is proportionate to the gravity of the potential breach of the Principles.

source_name: Australia Press Council, Statement of General Principles
tension_name: Individual-focused ethical obligations vs. harm to groups and corporate entities
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: Apply privacy, fairness, and harm-avoidance obligations only to named, identifiable individuals — treating harm to diffuse groups, communities, or organisations as outside the code's protective scope.
pole_b: Apply privacy, fairness, and harm-avoidance obligations to groups and categories of people — provided the group is reasonably specific and limited in number — and to corporations and other legal entities, not only to named individuals.
policy_text: 'Person' includes a group or category of people (provided it is reasonably specific and limited in number) and a corporation or other legal entity.

source_name: Camden Principles on Freedom of Expression and Equality (Article 19, 2009)
tension_name: Free expression vs. equality / combating discriminatory speech
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
