source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Verification rigour vs. publication speed
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish promptly using available sources and previously published material, accepting that full verification may not be possible under deadline pressure.
pole_b: Check facts as carefully as possible in light of the circumstances; remain critical of sources; do not rely on prior publication as a substitute for independent verification.
policy_text: Be critical of news sources. Check facts as carefully as possible in the light of the circumstances even if they have been published earlier.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Principled editorial judgment vs. mechanical rule-following
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: Follow the explicit rules of the code as written; treat rule compliance as the standard for ethical conduct.
pole_b: Treat ethics as a matter of responsible attitude and judgment; recognise that formal rules cannot substitute for genuine ethical reasoning in every situation.
policy_text: Ethics does not consist primarily of the application of a formal set of rules but in the maintenance of a responsible attitude in the exercise of journalistic duties.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Factual accuracy and transparency vs. individual privacy and naming restraint
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Report fully and accurately, including names, pictures, occupational details, and contextual identity markers that help the audience understand the story.
pole_b: Withhold names, pictures, and identifying details when publication might cause harm; ensure that omitting a name is not defeated by publishing details that enable identification anyway.
policy_text: Show careful consideration to the harmful consequences that might ensue for persons if their names are published. Refrain from publishing names if it might cause harm unless it is obviously in the public interest. / In case a person's name is not published, also refrain from publishing a picture of that person or details on occupation, title, age, nationality, sex, etc, which could enable identification.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Pre-publication right of reply vs. timeliness of publication
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish a story promptly when the facts are established, even if the criticised party has not yet had an opportunity to respond.
pole_b: Offer any person criticised in a factual report the opportunity to reply instantly and contemporaneously before publication; aim to present all parties' views.
policy_text: Offer persons, who are criticized in a factual report, the opportunity to reply instantly to the criticism. Aim at presenting the views of all parties involved.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Public interest in crime reporting vs. presumption of innocence and follow-up completeness
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully on alleged criminal conduct; the public has a legitimate interest in knowing about suspected wrongdoing even before a verdict.
pole_b: Treat suspects as innocent until proven guilty; report the outcome of a case whenever earlier coverage created a potentially negative impression of the individual.
policy_text: Remember that, in the eyes of the law, a person suspected of an offence is always presumed innocent until proven guilty. The outcome of a legal case should be published if it has been previously reported on.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Compelling visual journalism vs. accuracy and non-deception in image use
shared_tension_label: Accuracy and transparency in visual presentation vs. editorial/creative presentation needs
pole_a: Use images — including manipulated or illustrative composites — to tell the story visually, accepting that the line between illustration and reportage may blur.
pole_b: Verify that pictures are authentic; disclose any montage or retouching; ensure captions do not mislead; apply the same ethical standards to pictures as to text.
policy_text: Check the authenticity of pictures. See to it that pictures and graphical illustrations are correct and are not used in a misleading way. / Montage, electronic retouch and captions should be handled in such a way as not to mislead or deceive the reader. Whenever a picture has been altered through montage or retouch this should be stated.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Full contextual reporting vs. protection of effectively anonymous subjects
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Provide rich contextual detail — age, occupation, nationality, location, and other characteristics — to give readers a full and accurate picture of the people involved in a story.
pole_b: When a decision has been made not to name someone, withhold all identifying details (picture, occupation, title, age, nationality, sex) that would enable de facto identification.
policy_text: In case a person's name is not published, also refrain from publishing a picture of that person or details on occupation, title, age, nationality, sex, etc, which could enable identification. / Do not emphasize ethnic origin, sex, nationality, occupation, political affiliation, religious persuasion or sexual disposition… if this is not important in the specific context or is demeaning.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Outlet accountability transparency vs. reputational self-interest of publishers
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Manage criticism of the outlet's own past reporting discreetly; exercise editorial judgment about how prominently to feature regulatory rulings against the outlet; resist errors that attract public attention.
pole_b: Publish critical rulings of the Swedish Media Council concerning your own outlet without delay; publish corrections promptly and in a form that reaches those who received the original information.
policy_text: Publish without delay critical rulings issued by the Swedish Media Council in cases concerning your own newspaper. / Factual errors should be corrected when called for. Corrections and rebuttals shall be published promptly in appropriate form, in such a way that they will come to the attention of those who received the original information.

source_name: Code of Ethics for Press, Radio and Television in Sweden
tension_name: Full contextual identity reporting vs. avoiding irrelevant or demeaning identity markers
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Report all characteristics of the individuals involved in a story — ethnicity, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, occupation, political affiliation — as part of providing complete contextual information.
pole_b: Omit references to ethnic origin, sex, nationality, occupation, political affiliation, religious persuasion, or sexual disposition unless they are genuinely important in the specific context and their inclusion is not demeaning.
policy_text: Do not emphasize ethnic origin, sex, nationality, occupation, political affiliation, religious persuasion or sexual disposition in the case of the persons concerned if this is not important in the specific context or is demeaning.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Press freedom vs. voluntary ethical self-regulation
shared_tension_label: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Treat press freedom as absolute; resist all restrictions on collecting and disseminating news and comment, including those imposed by a code of ethics.
pole_b: Accept that press freedom is bounded by journalists' own voluntary self-regulation under the Code of Ethics; self-imposed ethical limits are the legitimate and preferred check on press freedom rather than state or commercial coercion.
policy_text: There shall be no restrictions regarding the collection and dissemination of news and comment. For the Press Council and its activities, the limits to this freedom are set by the journalists' voluntary self-regulation based on the provision of this Code of Ethics.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Speed of publication vs. accuracy and verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly to meet competitive or audience demands, even if verification is incomplete or a response has not been obtained from the subject of charges.
pole_b: Aim for maximum conscientiousness and accuracy; verify doubtful quotations before reproduction; seek a response before publishing charges; publish corrections promptly when errors emerge; follow up with important new developments after initial reporting.
policy_text: It is the prime duty of journalists to aim at a maximum of conscientiousness and accuracy in their investigations, the presentation of news items, and comments in them. / In case of serious doubts about the correctness of a quotation, the validity of third-party statements shall be checked before said statements are reproduced. / No charges shall be made against any person(s) or institution(s) unless proof can be furnished that an attempt has been made to obtain a statement on said charges from the person(s) or institution(s) so charged.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Correction obligation vs. institutional self-interest
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Minimise, delay, or suppress corrections to protect the publication's reputation, avoid legal exposure, or avoid conceding error.
pole_b: Publish corrections voluntarily, promptly, and as extensively as required, whether initiated by the editorial office itself or in response to a justified reader request.
policy_text: As soon as an editorial office is advised of the fact that it has published a wrong statement, professional ethics and common decency demand that a correction of a said statement be published voluntarily. / Any justified statement on the part of a reader or readers calling for correction of a report shall be published as soon as possible and as extensive as required.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Factual reporting vs. opinion and commentary — clear labelling
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Allow blended forms — fact-opinion hybrids, interpretive reporting, and embedded commentary — without formal labelling, trusting readers to infer the register.
pole_b: Ensure readers can always clearly distinguish factual reports, reproductions of third-party views, and commentary; this distinction is a structural requirement, not an aspiration.
policy_text: Readers shall be left in no doubts as to whether a newspaper item is a factual report, the reproduction of the views of a third party or third parties, or comment. / Photomontages and picture material that has been modified shall be clearly marked as such if a cursory reading might otherwise lead the reader to believe them to be documentary in nature.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Editorial independence vs. commercial and ownership pressure
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow advertiser interests, ownership preferences, or commercial considerations to shape the form, content, or emphasis of editorial material — overtly or subtly.
pole_b: Keep editorial content entirely free from outside interests; the publisher's economic interests must never produce wrong information or suppress important stories; journalists' private and commercial interests must have no bearing on editorial content.
policy_text: Form and content of contributions to the editorial sections of a newspaper or magazine shall on no account be influenced by outside interests. / The publishers' economic interests shall not affect editorial content in any way that might result in wrong information or the suppression of important information. / The press is just able to fulfil the special responsibility towards the public, if private as well as commercial interests of media employees have no bearing on the editorial content.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Anti-gifts rule vs. conditional acceptance (press trips and personal advantages)
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept gifts, free travel, hospitality, and other personal advantages from sources, PR representatives, or interested parties as normal professional practice without disclosure.
pole_b: Refuse all personal advantages that are likely to influence the journalistic product; if a journey has been paid for by a third party and a report is published, disclose this fact to readers in a suitable way.
policy_text: Any person who accepts, in the context of his/her work as a journalist, presents or any other personal advantages likely to influence the journalistic product shall be deemed to have breached this Code of Ethics. / If a journalist publishes a report on a journey, which has been paid for by a third party, this fact shall be mentioned in the report in a suitable way.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Child and juvenile protection vs. transparency about crime and public events
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Report on crimes and misconduct involving juveniles with the same transparency — including names and photographs — applied to adult subjects, on the grounds that the public has an interest in knowing about crime in its community.
pole_b: Give absolute precedence to a child's privacy over news value; apply special critical scrutiny before publishing any pictures or reports about juveniles; never publish a juvenile's full name in connection with criminal offences; exercise particular caution in interviewing and photographing children to avoid detrimental effects on their future.
policy_text: In the case of children, protection of the individual's privacy shall take precedence over the news value. / Reports about criminal offences or misconduct on the part of juveniles shall not render more difficult or completely prevent their eventual re-integration into society. In such cases, the individual's full name shall not be published. / Journalists shall exercise particular caution in interviewing and photographing children and in reporting about matters which might have a detrimental influence on their future.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Fair newsgathering methods vs. investigative public interest
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever investigative methods — including misrepresentation, hidden recording, or undercover operations — are necessary to expose wrongdoing in the public interest.
pole_b: Obtain evidence only by fair and proper means; improper methods including misrepresentation, pressure, intimidation, exploitation of emotional distress, and wiretapping are prohibited as a default; undercover investigation is a narrow exception requiring both proportionality and genuine public interest.
policy_text: No unfair or improper methods shall be used in obtaining oral or procuring written evidence. / Unfair or improper methods shall include misrepresentation, pressure, intimidation, exploitation of emotional or stressful situations and, as a rule, the use of wiretapping or bugging equipment. / In some cases undercover investigations and the associated actions deemed necessary are permitted, provided that the method of the recherché is appropriate and the gathered information is in the public interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Restraint in suicide coverage vs. duty to inform the public
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Treat suicide and self-harm as newsworthy events deserving full reporting; the public's right to information and freedom of the press extend to all matters of human experience including death.
pole_b: Treat media coverage of suicides and self-harm with much reserve; because of the documented danger of imitation, weigh carefully whether the information is in the public interest and avoid exaggerated reporting.
policy_text: Media coverage on suicides and self-inflicted injury as well as on suicide attempts and attempts of self-inflicted injury has to be treated with much reserve. Especially because of the danger of imitation, responsible-minded journalists weigh up if the information is in the public interest and abstain from exaggerated reporting.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press
tension_name: Freedom of religious and ideological criticism vs. protection from disparagement
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Treat religious teachings, institutions, and ideologies as fully open to critical journalism, satire, and commentary — including content that members of those communities find offensive.
pole_b: Refrain from disparaging or deriding religious teachings or recognised churches and religious communities in ways that are liable to give justified offence; avoid sweeping generalisations that disparage or incite suspicion against any person or group.
policy_text: Any disparagement or derision of religious teachings or recognized churches and religious communities liable to give justified offence shall be inadmissible. / Sweeping statements which disparage or incite suspicion against a person or group of persons shall be strictly avoided.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
shared_tension_label: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish freely; treat freedom of communication as the paramount value and resist any restriction on gathering and disseminating information.
pole_b: Exercise press freedom only within the limits of the law and only in ways that do not unduly harm individual reputation without sufficient public-interest justification.
policy_text: Freedom of communication is the basic premise for a working democratic society, and the free press the means and prerequisite for attaining it. / Provided it remains within the limits of the law, the free press and other media may not be restricted or obstructed in the gathering and publication of information. / The reputation of any individual shall not be unduly harmed without there being sufficient evidence that the information regarding that person is in the public interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Speed and completeness of publication vs. accuracy and verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly and comprehensively to satisfy the public's right to timely information, accepting that full verification may lag behind.
pole_b: Verify accuracy and source reliability — especially for controversial materials and non-staff contributions — before publication, even if this delays or limits what is published.
policy_text: Media organisations shall undertake to prevent the publication of inaccurate, distorted or misleading information. / The editors shall, especially in the case of controversial materials, confirm the accuracy of the information and the reliability of the sources. / News material shall be based on verifiable factual evidence.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Transparent identification in newsgathering vs. covert/undercover methods
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use covert or deceptive means to gather information when the story is important and a source would not cooperate if approached openly.
pole_b: Always identify yourself and your outlet when conducting interviews and use honest means to obtain recordings and information.
policy_text: When conducting interviews, journalists must always identify themselves and the media outlet they represent. / A journalist shall use honest means of obtaining audio or video recordings and information, with the exception of cases where the public has a right to know information that cannot be obtained in an honest way.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. source transparency and verifiability
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Disclose source identities or refuse to publish unverified anonymous claims in the interest of transparency and editorial accountability.
pole_b: Protect the identity of confidential sources as a moral obligation, even when doing so limits the public's ability to assess source reliability.
policy_text: Media outlets have a moral obligation to safeguard the identity of confidential sources of information. / The editors shall, especially in the case of controversial materials, confirm the accuracy of the information and the reliability of the sources. / Journalists must strictly keep any promises made to their sources.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Public accountability reporting vs. individual reputation and presumption of innocence
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully on alleged wrongdoing, charges, and criminal proceedings in the public interest, naming those involved and describing the alleged conduct.
pole_b: Do not treat any individual as a criminal before a court sentence; do not unduly harm reputation without sufficient public-interest evidence; consider carefully whether identification is necessary and what suffering it causes.
policy_text: The media shall not treat any individual as a criminal prior to a court sentence to that effect. / The reputation of any individual shall not be unduly harmed without there being sufficient evidence that the information regarding that person is in the public interest. / When covering crime, court cases and accidents, the journalist shall consider whether the identification of the parties involved is necessary and what suffering it may cause to them. / Victims and juvenile offenders shall not be identified as a general rule.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Public's right to know vs. individual privacy
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish all information the public has an interest in knowing, including details about individuals' private lives, health, family disputes, and personal circumstances.
pole_b: Disseminate privacy-violating material only when public interest demonstrably outweighs the individual's right to privacy; default to non-disclosure for health information, child custody matters, and similar intimate subjects.
policy_text: Materials violating the privacy of an individual can only be disseminated if public interest outweighs the right to privacy. / Information and speculation about an individual's mental or physical health shall not be disseminated unless the individual is willing or the information is in the public interest. / As a rule, child custody battles should not be covered.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Editorial authority vs. individual journalist conscience and outside-contributor autonomy
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Editors and media organisations have final authority over what is published, how it is edited, and what assignments journalists undertake — individual objections are subordinate to editorial direction.
pole_b: Editorial staff may not be compelled to write or perform activities that contradict their personal convictions; outside contributors' content, context, and intended release time should not be altered without their knowledge and consent.
policy_text: Editorial staff members may not be obliged by their employer to write or perform any similar activity contradicting their personal convictions. / The content, context and intended time of release of materials submitted by an outside contributor should not be altered without the author's knowledge and consent.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Commercial imperatives vs. editorial independence and transparency
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow commercial relationships, product coverage, and promotional activity to blend with editorial content in order to sustain the media outlet financially.
pole_b: Clearly differentiate advertisements from editorial content; journalists must not air commercials or write promotional articles in the same outlet; product mentions in editorial material require genuine journalistic justification; consumer journalism must disclose methodology.
policy_text: Advertisements and promotional materials shall be clearly differentiated from editorial material. / Journalists and regular outside contributors should not air commercials within their programme, or write promotional articles under their own name in the same publication. / A product or trademark shall be mentioned or displayed in news and other editorial material only if relevant and justified. / In the case of consumer-oriented journalistic material, the audience must be informed how the selection of the products was made and how the products were tested.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Child and vulnerable-source protection vs. public-interest coverage involving minors
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Cover stories involving minors and media-inexperienced sources in the same way as any other story, treating news value and the public's right to know as the primary filter.
pole_b: Default to strong protection: do not interview minors without parental consent; do not identify juvenile offenders or victims; do not cover child custody battles; warn media-inexperienced sources of consequences before conversations begin.
policy_text: Minors shall be interviewed, as a general rule, only in the presence of or with the consent of the parent or guardian. / Journalists may not take advantage of people lacking experience in relating to the media. The possible consequences of their statements shall be explained prior to the conversation. / As a rule, child custody battles should not be covered. / Victims and juvenile offenders shall not be identified as a general rule.

source_name: Code of Ethics for the Estonian Press
tension_name: Immediate right of rebuttal vs. publication freedom and deadline constraints
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish serious accusations when ready, offering the accused a chance to respond after publication through a formal right-of-reply process.
pole_b: Offer individuals subjected to serious accusations an opportunity for immediate rebuttal in the same edition or programme before or simultaneously with publication.
policy_text: Individuals subjected to serious accusations should be offered an opportunity for immediate rebuttal in the same edition or programme. / In the case of materials concerning a controversy, the journalist shall hear all sides of the conflict. / A correction shall be issued in the event of any inaccuracies.

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Verify-before-publish vs. disclose-and-publish-unverified
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish information that has not been fully verified, without alerting the audience to its unverified status.
pole_b: Verify all information before publishing; if verification is genuinely impossible despite all reasonable measures and the information is of public significance, publish with a clear disclosure to the audience of its unverified status.
policy_text: Prior to publishing, to check the accuracy of information from any source, not to conceal or distort facts, and not to publish obviously false information; / Clearly notify the audience about the cases when the editorial office received information of public significance, but has been unable to verify the facts after employing all the reasonable measures;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Identify sources vs. protect confidential sources
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Withhold source identification routinely or promise confidentiality freely without prior justification.
pole_b: Identify sources to the extent possible; avoid using confidential sources where possible; justify any confidentiality promise before making it; once promised, never disclose the source under any circumstances.
policy_text: To the extent possible, specify the sources of information; / To the extent possible, avoid using confidential sources of information and, before promising to keep the source of information confidential, always justify that decision. / if the provision of information is conditioned upon keeping the source confidential, never to disclose the source;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Avoid covert methods vs. serve the public interest through investigation
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use covert or secret information-gathering methods as a standard journalistic tool without justification.
pole_b: Use only open methods by default; resort to covert methods only when open methods cannot yield information of public interest; in all such cases, explain and justify the use of covert methods in the actual publication.
policy_text: To avoid the use of covert and secret methods of obtaining information, except when traditional open methods do not ensure receipt of information of public interest. The need for such methods must be explained and justified in the actual publication;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Editorial independence vs. interviewee co-authorship rights
shared_tension_label: Editorial independence vs. Subject approval rights
pole_a: Treat the finished interview text as entirely within the journalist's editorial control, with no special rights accorded to the interviewee over the published version.
pole_b: Respect the rights of the interviewee in regard to the interview text, treating them as its co-author.
policy_text: To respect rights of interviewee in regard to the text of the interview, as its coauthor.

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Privacy of private individuals vs. public's right to be informed
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish all available private information about individuals when it is accurate and newsworthy, regardless of whether a public-interest justification exists.
pole_b: Respect and protect the right to private life; only publish private information when justified by public interest or its protection, and even then only regarding high-ranking officials, public figures, and those aspiring to power or public attention.
policy_text: To respect and protect the human right to private life, including respect to personal and family life, residence, property, health condition, correspondence. Only public interest or protection thereof can justify publication of information regarding the privacy of high rank officials, public figures, and individuals aspiring to power or public attention;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Presumption of innocence vs. public's right to know about crime suspects
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Publish the names of all crime suspects before trial as a matter of course, treating the public's right to know as automatically overriding the presumption of innocence.
pole_b: Respect the presumption of innocence; before publishing the name of a crime suspect prior to trial, specifically weigh the public need for doing so against the suspect's right to a fair trial and to the presumption of innocence.
policy_text: To respect the presumption of innocence: when publishing the names of crime suspects before the trial, to consider the public need for doing so - strike a balance between the presumption of innocence, the right of crime suspects to fair trial, and the right of the public to be informed.

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Free exchange of opinions vs. prohibition of hate speech and harmful advocacy
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Allow all opinions to be expressed and published regardless of their content, treating free expression as an absolute value.
pole_b: Encourage free exchange of opinions regardless of difference from editorial views, but categorically exclude hate speech, promotion of ethnic or religious hatred and intolerance, discrimination, pornography, violence, war, and genocide denial.
policy_text: To encourage free exchange of opinions, regardless of any differences between those opinions and the editorial views; / Not to promote in any way ethnic or religious hatred and intolerance, or any discrimination on political, social, sexual, and language grounds, exclude hate speech; / Not to advocate pornography, violence, war, in any form; not to deny genocide and crimes against humanity;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Commercial and owner interests vs. editorial independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow advertisers, sponsors, and owners to influence editorial coverage in exchange for commercial benefit; accept benefits that secure ongoing commercial relationships.
pole_b: Resist all pressure by advertisers, sponsors, and owners to influence coverage; refuse payments, gifts, and benefits given in exchange for publishing or suppressing information; give no editorial advantage to advertisers; label all paid content; when systemic pressure threatens to become a public challenge, inform the public and call for community support.
policy_text: To resist pressure by advertisers, sponsors, and media owners aimed at influencing the coverage of events. Whenever this sort of pressure threatens to become a public challenge, inform the public about the situation, calling for the support of journalists and the community; / To refuse payments, gifts, awards, compensations, free holidays and other benefits promised in return to publishing or not publishing information, contradicting professional independence, compromising journalist's reputation and resulting in a loss of trust towards the media; / To give no advantage to advertisers and sponsors in editorial pieces; / To draw a clear line between journalistic materials and advertisement...

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Right of response and correction vs. editorial independence and investigative integrity
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Treat published materials as final editorial products with no obligation to engage with subjects' objections, correct errors, or offer response opportunities.
pole_b: Provide all subjects of criticism and accusation an opportunity to respond; admit mistakes and be ready to correct them; be ready to meet with persons who feel offended or defamed.
policy_text: To be ready to meet with persons or representatives of organizations who feel offended or defamed by a certain publication, and provide an opportunity of response for all those against who criticism and accusations have been made in the publications; / To admit mistakes and to be ready to correct them;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Broadcast neutrality vs. print/online editorial endorsement in elections
shared_tension_label: Broadcast neutrality vs. print/online editorial endorsement in elections
pole_a: Allow all media platforms, including broadcast, to editorially support candidates or parties during elections without disclosure or constraint.
pole_b: Require broadcast media to remain strictly neutral; allow print and online media to support a candidate or party only with clear advance announcement of intent; prohibit hidden political advertising across all platforms; give all candidates equal access and equal tariffs.
policy_text: Broadcast media must refrain from supporting any specific candidate or party, and the print and online media must provide clear advance announcement of their intent to do so. / Not to publish materials containing hidden political advertising, and to separate materials presented for (free or paid) publication by groups supporting any party or candidate or produced at their request from other materials, or to make mention about it; / To give all candidates equal possibilities for presenting their platforms and views in the media, and to apply single tariffs when allocating paid space or air time in media;

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Comprehensive terrorism and conflict reporting vs. harm avoidance and sympathy prohibition
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report on terrorism and violent conflict comprehensively and without restriction, treating the public's right to know as overriding all harm concerns.
pole_b: Be careful when disseminating information about terrorist acts; rule out content that may instil sympathy toward terrorists; treat witnesses delicately as information sources; protect the identity of relatives and friends of hostages and victims without their consent.
policy_text: To be careful when disseminating information about terrorist acts, to rule out content and reports that may instill sympathy towards terrorists, to treat witnesses of events as sources of information delicately, and avoid disclosing the identity of relatives or friends of hostages and possible victims without their consent.

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Child protection and informed consent vs. newsworthiness and documentary public interest
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Treat children as reportable subjects like any other, prioritising newsworthiness and speed of documentation over consent and protection obligations.
pole_b: Obtain consent from both child and guardian before interviewing, filming, or photographing; prefer written consent; ensure no coercion; explain potential global dissemination; avoid reactivating trauma; refuse to make children perform for dramatic effect; follow UNICEF guidelines throughout.
policy_text: Obtain permission from the child and his/her guardian for all interviews, videotaping and for documentary photographs. When possible and appropriate, this permission should be in writing. Permission must be obtained in circumstances that ensure that the child and guardian are not coerced in any way and that they understand that they are part of a story that might be disseminated locally and globally.

source_name: Code of Ethics of Armenian Media and Journalists
tension_name: Accuracy and transparency in visual presentation vs. editorial/creative presentation needs
shared_tension_label: Accuracy and transparency in visual presentation vs. editorial/creative presentation needs
pole_a: Use technical manipulation of photos and video freely for editorial and aesthetic purposes without disclosure to the audience.
pole_b: Ensure that photo, video, and audio materials correspond to reality; use headlines that derive from content; use citations in context; disclose any technical tricks used in photos or video.
policy_text: To ensure that the reports, photo, video and audio materials correspond to the reality, the headlines derive from the content of the material, citations are not used outside of context... / Not to distort the content of photo or video materials, to mention about technical tricks in photos and video materials if any.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Accuracy vs. Audience and Victim Harm
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Publish fully accurate, unfiltered depictions of death, violence, crime, and vulnerability because truthful completeness best serves the public's right to know.
pole_b: Calibrate the accuracy and graphic detail of reporting on violence, crime, and vulnerable persons to avoid gratuitous harm to audiences, victims' families, and people with disabilities or illness.
policy_text: It is unacceptable to show scenes of death in close-up, and the bloody effects of wars and catastrophes; manifestations of cruelty and violence can be described and shown only on condition of maintaining a balance between the accuracy of the reporting and the sensitivity of the audience's feelings, especially victims' families and their relatives. / Consideration must be exercised to not offend people with physical or mental disabilities, the old and the sick, and those who are helpless in life.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Investigative Truth-Seeking vs. Privacy
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use covert methods and intrude into private or intimate spheres when doing so is necessary to expose crime, corruption, or abuse of power on behalf of the public good.
pole_b: Respect the private and intimate sphere of all individuals as a default; refrain from covert surveillance and privacy intrusion in ordinary journalistic practice.
policy_text: The private and intimate sphere must not be violated; in justified circumstances, an exception can include activities in the field of investigative journalism, and also for public figures. / hidden cameras and microphones or telephone wiretapping are permissible only in the case of investigative journalism, i.e. tracking of crimes, corruption, or abuse of power, on behalf of the public good and with the knowledge and consent of the journalist's superiors.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Editorial Independence vs. Institutional Loyalty
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Follow the instructions of supervisors, publishers, and broadcasters as the default condition of professional employment.
pole_b: Refuse any instruction that contradicts law, professional ethics, or the journalist's well-established convictions, regardless of hierarchical pressure.
policy_text: The journalist is loyal to his supervisors and publishers or broadcasters. However, they cannot order the journalist, and the journalist has the right to refuse, to carry out orders contrary to the law, their professional ethics, or well-established convictions. / Opinions may be biased, but they must not distort the facts and be the result of external pressures.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Opinion Freedom vs. Respect and Non-Distortion Constraint
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Permit genuinely held critical opinions, even if they are harsh, provided the underlying facts are accurate and the opinion does not stem from external pressure.
pole_b: Ensure that critical opinions do not cross into disrespect for subjects, distortion of facts, or results of external pressure; always show respect for persons regardless of ideological, cultural, or moral differences.
policy_text: Opinions may be biased, but they must not distort the facts and be the result of external pressures. / A journalist should show respect for people, regardless of their ideological, cultural, or moral differences which do not comply with the journalist's own views.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Commercial and Political Independence vs. Access and Institutional Pressure
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept gifts, free travel, advertising assignments, or political roles when they are necessary to sustain relationships, access, or the financial viability of the outlet.
pole_b: Decline all gifts above the PLN 200 threshold, refuse involvement in advertising, public relations, and political activity, and never use professionally obtained information for personal gain, in order to preserve journalistic credibility and independence.
policy_text: Journalistic credibility and independence are incompatible with accepting gifts worth more than PLN 200, free trips, or items and devices for testing. / A journalist cannot be involved in canvassing or participate in advertising and public relations; the only exception is social and charity campaigns; editorial materials must be clearly separated from advertising and promotional materials. / Surreptitious advertising and withholding of information are highly reprehensible. / A journalist may not use publicly disclosed information obtained in the course of their professional activity for their own interest, especially in financial and economic journalism. / The involvement of journalists in direct political and party activity is also a manifestation of a conflict of interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Presumption of Innocence vs. Public's Right to Know About Crime
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report crime fully and specifically — naming suspects, describing evidence, and detailing the alleged offence — so the public can hold the justice system to account.
pole_b: Exercise extreme caution when identifying suspects and describing crimes; treat all persons as innocent until a court issues a final judgment; avoid descriptions that could incite anti-social acts.
policy_text: When disclosing crimes and persons suspected of having committed crimes, extreme caution should be exercised to avoid descriptions that allow for initiation of anti-social acts, and not presume guilt until the court issues a final judgment.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Proactive Self-Correction vs. Reputational and Commercial Self-Interest
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Correct errors only when requested by affected parties, fault has been established, or there is a legal obligation — avoid proactive self-correction that draws attention to mistakes.
pole_b: Immediately correct all errors and mistakes upon discovery, regardless of who is at fault, whether anyone has complained, or what the reputational cost may be.
policy_text: Errors and mistakes require immediate rectification, even if they were not the fault of the author or the editors and regardless of whether anyone applied for rectification.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Association of Polish Journalists
tension_name: Informed Consent vs. Newsworthiness
shared_tension_label: Informed Consent vs. Newsworthiness
pole_a: Publish newsworthy statements made by individuals, including children, without seeking specific consent, treating the act of speaking to a journalist as implicit consent.
pole_b: Inform interviewees about the use of their statements; obtain permission when an interviewee restricts use; never use children's statements without parental or guardian consent.
policy_text: Interviewees should be informed about the use of their statements; permission is required from the interviewee if the interviewee restricts the use of their statements; children's statements may only be used with the consent of their parents or legal guardians.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Speed vs. Verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish information quickly, before full verification, to meet competitive and audience-timeliness demands.
pole_b: Endeavour to verify information using multiple sources before publication; always signal when information remains unconfirmed; never knowingly publish inaccuracies.
policy_text: We shall endeavour to verify information, as we look for and use different sources, before it is published, and we shall indicate its provenance where appropriate. / We shall always indicate where information has not been confirmed. / We shall not publish information we know to be inaccurate.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Source Transparency vs. Source Protection
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use anonymous sources freely; do not reveal who provided information even when this limits the public's ability to assess credibility.
pole_b: Prefer identified sources so the public can assess honesty and reliability; indicate provenance where appropriate; but protect the identity of sources who provided information in confidence.
policy_text: We prefer to use identified sources rather than anonymous sources, as the latter's honesty and reliability cannot be assessed by the public. / We shall protect the identity of confidential sources of information. / We shall endeavour to verify information, as we look for and use different sources, before it is published, and we shall indicate its provenance where appropriate.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Fair/Open Newsgathering vs. Investigative Necessity (Subterfuge)
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use deceptive or covert newsgathering methods — hidden cameras, false identity, subterfuge — as a convenient tool of investigative journalism.
pole_b: Gather information exclusively by fair and legal means; resort to subterfuge only when no other means exist to obtain information of exceptional public importance, and disclose those methods in the published story.
policy_text: We shall gather information by fair and legal means. / We shall only make use of subterfuge, hidden cameras, microphones, and other special equipment or means, including obscuring our professional identity, if there are no other means to obtain information deemed exceptionally important to the public interest; we shall indicate such methods in the respective story.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Privacy vs. Public Accountability
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish whatever information about individuals is newsworthy, regardless of their privacy interests, treating public curiosity as sufficient justification.
pole_b: Respect the inviolability of private life as a default; intrude into private and family life only when an exceptional circumstance genuinely important to the public interest justifies it; apply a stricter standard to non-public figures than to those who have voluntarily entered public life.
policy_text: We respect the inviolability of everyone's private life. / Only an exceptional circumstance that is important to the public interest would justify the media's intrusion into private and family life. / According to the jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights, public figures can expect a lesser degree of privacy; however, information about their private lives can be disclosed only if it serves the public interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Heightened Child Protection vs. Children's Right to Be Heard
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Engage children freely as journalistic subjects and sources, treating their participation as equivalent to adult participation.
pole_b: Apply a heightened standard of care to all child-related journalism — protect their identity, do not exploit their innocence and trust, require adult consent before interviewing, and avoid publishing their private information unless an overriding public interest exists — while also respecting their right to be heard.
policy_text: We shall demonstrate special responsibility in respecting the rights of children, including their right to be heard. / We shall not take advantage of a child's innocence and trust. / We shall seek to avoid interviewing children without the consent of an adult in charge. / We shall not publish information or photographs about the private life of a child unless there is an overriding circumstance serving the public interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Full Crime and Tragedy Reporting vs. Victim and Witness Protection
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Report on crime and tragedy with complete detail — identify all participants, describe all methods, cover all outcomes — to fully inform the public.
pole_b: Report with sympathy and restraint; protect the identity of victims and witnesses (especially in sexual assault cases and where children are involved); respect the presumption of innocence; do not glorify or unnecessarily sensationalise; follow up on trial outcomes when charges have been reported.
policy_text: We respect the assumption of innocence and will not describe a person as a criminal prior to the person's conviction. / We shall treat with caution the identification of victims and witnesses of crime, especially in cases involving sexual assault, unless the respective victims and witnesses give consent to being identified. / We shall refrain from glorifying or unnecessarily sensationalising crime, violence, and brutality when reporting them. / We shall not add to the distress of people affected by tragedy or crime and shall report such matters with sympathy and constraint.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial/Political Sustainability
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow political owners, advertisers, sponsors, and commercial pressures to shape editorial decisions, accepting that media viability depends on these relationships.
pole_b: Resist all political and commercial pressure; maintain a strict separation between editorial decision-making and commercial policy; clearly distinguish editorial content from advertising and sponsored material; decline inducements; avoid covering stories where you have a direct personal interest, or declare that interest.
policy_text: We shall not be susceptible to political or commercial pressure or influence. / We shall maintain a clear distinction between editorial decision making, and the commercial policy of the media. / We shall maintain a clear distinction between editorial content, and marketing, advertisements, or sponsored materials. / We shall not accept any personal, political, or financial inducements that may impact our ability to provide the public with accurate information.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Professional Solidarity vs. Truth and Information Integrity
shared_tension_label: Professional solidarity vs. accountability for unethical colleagues
pole_a: Always support colleagues publicly regardless of the merits of criticism against them, treating solidarity as an unconditional professional value.
pole_b: Support colleagues when they are unfairly attacked; but professional solidarity must never become an excuse for suppressing or distorting information, and media outlets have an institutional duty to support journalists who respected this code but face legal action.
policy_text: We shall support media colleagues when they are unfairly attacked or criticised. However, professional solidarity should not be an excuse for suppressing or distorting information.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Informing the Public About Violence and Extremism vs. Not Platforming Violence
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report fully and without restriction on violent movements, extremist groups, and those who incite violence, treating all such reporting as straightforwardly in the public interest.
pole_b: Avoid publishing material that incites or encourages hatred, violence, or discrimination; take care not to become a platform for those who promote violence; report on such activities only with due constraint and only when it clearly serves the public interest.
policy_text: We respect everyone's right to live in safety and security, and we shall avoid publishing material that incites or encourages hatred, violence, or any form of discrimination. / We shall be careful not to be used as a platform for those who would promote, incite, or otherwise use violence; we shall report on such activities with due constraint and only if it clearly serves the public interest.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Genuine Public Interest vs. Public Curiosity (Audience Appeal)
shared_tension_label: The public-interest test: genuine public interest vs. curiosity and proportionality
pole_a: Treat what audiences find interesting, entertaining, or curious as sufficient justification for publishing — equating "interesting to the public" with "in the public interest."
pole_b: Apply a rigorous distinction between what is genuinely in the public interest (protects health/safety/security; prevents/discloses serious crime or abuse of power; prevents serious public deception) and what is merely interesting or entertaining to audiences; any infringement of the code's terms must be clearly and fully demonstrated to serve the best interests of the public.
policy_text: Infringement of the terms of this Code may only be justified where it can be clearly and fully demonstrated that the respective publication serves the best interests of the public. / For the purposes of this Code, information that is in, of, serves, or is otherwise important to 'the public interest' should not be confused with information that is 'interesting to the public.'

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Correction and Accountability vs. Reputational Protection of the Outlet
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Minimise, delay, bury, or omit corrections to protect the outlet's reputation and avoid admitting error.
pole_b: When inaccurate or misleading information has been published and this can be demonstrated, publish a clear and appropriately prominent correction; provide a right of reply to directly affected individuals and organisations; apologise if necessary.
policy_text: We shall publish a clear and appropriately prominent correction when it can be demonstrated that inaccurate or misleading information has been published, and we shall provide an apology if necessary. / We shall provide a right of reply to individuals and organisations directly affected by inaccurate or misleading publications.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Conscience Clause (Individual Journalist's Refusal) vs. Editorial Authority
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Editorial and management authority over journalists is absolute; journalists must complete all assigned work regardless of ethical objection.
pole_b: Individual journalists have a right to refuse assignments — or refuse to be identified as the author of publications — that would break the letter and spirit of this code; media outlets must support journalists who are legally challenged for compliant code work.
policy_text: We respect the right of individual journalists to refuse, or refuse being identified as the author of, assignments or publications which would break the letter and spirit of this Code. / We believe that individual journalists who respected the letter and spirit of this Code yet are charged in court by third parties should be supported by their respective media outlet.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Bulgarian Media
tension_name: Attribution and Intellectual Honesty vs. Speed and Aggregation in Digital Publishing
shared_tension_label: Attribution / anti-plagiarism vs. speed and aggregation pressure
pole_a: In fast-moving digital publishing, use material from other outlets without attribution, rewrite or aggregate without acknowledging sources, and treat copyright compliance as a secondary concern.
pole_b: Plagiarism is unacceptable in all forms and circumstances; respect copyright; always acknowledge the source of short extracts used without express permission; obtain prior permission and acknowledgement for longer extracts or complete works; maintain mutual respect and fair competition between media outlets.
policy_text: We consider all forms of plagiarism to be unacceptable in all circumstances. / We respect copyright and the terms of copyright agreements. / We shall always acknowledge the source of short extracts of material from other media which may be in use without their express permission. / We shall only reproduce longer extracts or complete materials from other media with the prior permission and acknowledgement of the respective author and media.

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Latin American Federation of Journalists (FELAP)
tension_name: Press freedom as expansive right vs. press freedom as bounded by people's interests
shared_tension_label: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Press freedom is an absolute or near-absolute right that cannot legitimately be restricted by any external authority, including popular or state authority acting in the people's name.
pole_b: Press freedom is the people's right to be informed accurately and in a timely way; it may be restricted by "the interests of the people" themselves, and its exercise must be responsible and non-abusive.
policy_text: Freedom of the press is the right of our people to be informed in a timely and accurate manner, and to express their opinions without restrictions other than those imposed by the interests of those very people. (Preamble) / Freedom of information requires as an indispensable element the willingness and capacity to employ its privileges without abuse. (Preamble, citing UN Res. 59(I))

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Latin American Federation of Journalists (FELAP)
tension_name: Editorial independence from commercial pressures vs. structural dependence on commercial media ownership
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept that commercial media structures and ownership imperatives necessarily shape journalistic output, and work within those constraints.
pole_b: Resist commercial conversion of news into merchandise; insist on editorial independence from commercial, advertising, and ownership pressures; reject conflation of journalistic identity with media ownership.
policy_text: FELAP recognizes that it is difficult to apply an ethical standard to a system governed by private ownership of the media, where news is converted into merchandise. (Preamble) / In the diffusion of ideas and opinions, journalists will appraise the conditions so that they can express themselves in a democratic fashion and not be limited by commercial, advertising, or other interests. (Art. 4) / media owners usurp our name, calling themselves 'journalists,' and they apply ethical rules that are governed by the search for commercial benefit. (Preamble)

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Latin American Federation of Journalists (FELAP)
tension_name: Honest reporting on armed conflict vs. rejection of war propaganda
shared_tension_label: Honest reporting on armed conflict vs. rejection of war propaganda
pole_a: Report honestly and fully on armed conflict, including on the military, strategic, and political logic of the use of force, without sanitising the reality of war.
pole_b: Reject propaganda on the inevitability of war and the use of force; use journalism to strengthen peace, co-existence, and international cooperation.
policy_text: To reject propaganda on the inevitability of war, threats, and the use of force in international conflicts. (Art. 3) / Journalism should contribute to the strengthening of peace, co-existence, self-determination of the people, disarmament, international cooperation, and mutual understanding among all the peoples of the world. (Art. 2)

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Latin American Federation of Journalists (FELAP)
tension_name: National/decolonial cultural orientation vs. universal impartiality across cultures
shared_tension_label: National/decolonial cultural orientation vs. universal impartiality across cultures
pole_a: Report on all cultures, nations, and groups with equal impartiality, without privileging one cultural or national frame.
pole_b: Actively defend national values, language, and cultural identity; fight for Latin American economic, political, and cultural independence; promote decolonisation of information.
policy_text: It is the inalienable right of Latin American journalists to contribute to the economic, political, and cultural independence of our nations and towns, to the establishment of a New International Economic Order, and to the decolonisation of information. (Art. 2) / will seek to defend national values, especially the value of language as a cultural expression and as an important factor in new forms of culture. (Art. 10)

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Latin American Federation of Journalists (FELAP)
tension_name: Defamation prohibition vs. duty to report truthfully on powerful figures
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Withhold or soften reporting on powerful individuals or institutions to avoid legal or reputational claims of defamation or slander.
pole_b: Report truthfully and fully on individuals and institutions in the public interest, even when those subjects may characterise accurate reporting as defamatory.
policy_text: Defamation and slander. (Art. 7, violations list) / Journalists will adopt the principles of truth and objectivity in their work and will commit ethical faults when they silence, falsify or manipulate facts. (Art. 4) / To fight for a new information order that relates to the people's interests and that replaces the one which currently exists in the majority of Latin American countries and deforms reality. (Art. 3)

source_name: Code of Ethics of the Norwegian Press (Vær Varsom-plakaten)
tension_name: Press freedom vs. individual privacy and protection
shared_tension_label: Press freedom vs. legal and reputational constraint
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a:
** Publish freely and fully in the exercise of press freedom, prioritising the public's right to information over the private interests of individuals.
**Pole A provenance:** directly stated in code (arts. 1.01, 1.02, 1.04, 1.05)

**Pole B (higher / more policy-aligned):** Restrict or qualify publication where it would unjustifiably intrude on privacy, stigmatise individuals, or expose them to disproportionate harm.
**Pole B provenance:** directly stated in code (arts. 4.03, 4.06, 4.07, 4.08, 4.09)

**Gold (from this source's view):** B — but the code frames B not as a suppression of A, it frames B as the contextually appropriate exercise of A. The code holds both poles in structured tension with proportionality tests, not a flat hierarchy; however, where they genuinely conflict, the publication rules (Section 4) consistently impose restraint as the duty, making B the policy-aligned pole.

**Suggested policy_text:**
Original: *"It is the right of the press to carry information on what goes on in society and to uncover and disclose matters, which ought to be subjected to criticism."* / *"Always respect a person character and identity, privacy, ethnicity, nationality and belief. Be careful when using terms that create stigmas. Never draw attention to personal or private aspects if they are irrelevant."*
EN gloss: The press has an affirmative right—and duty—to investigate and publish matters of public concern, but must always weigh that right against respect for individual character, identity, and privacy, publishing personal details only where they are relevant.

**Scenarios (drawn from verbatim where possible):**
S-A: A reporter documents how a public institution has failed individuals in its care (art. 1.05). Publishing the story serves the press's protective function, even though named individuals within the institution may suffer reputational harm.
S-B: A story about a crime victim includes details about their ethnicity and personal history that are not relevant to the wrongdoing being reported. Art. 4.03 requires omitting these details even though they are available.
S-C: A childcare dispute involves genuine public interest in how an authority treated a family. Art. 4.08 establishes a general rule against identifying the children involved, even where a parent has consented, because the implications for the child must be separately assessed.

**L2 exceptions (from CONDITIONS / EXCEPTIONS):**
- Personal or private details may be reported when they are relevant (entry #35)
- Identification in criminal matters is legitimate when there is imminent danger of assault on defenceless individuals, in serious and repeated crimes, when identity is patently relevant, or when it protects the innocent from unjustified suspicion (entry #41)
- Even parental consent does not automatically permit identification of children in family or childcare proceedings; implications must still be assessed independently (entry #42)
- Suicide reporting is permissible when it meets a genuine general informational need, but description of methods is prohibited regardless of newsworthiness (entry #43)

**Pressures the code addresses:**
Consensus stakes (legitimate pressures toward Pole B):
- Subject is a minor or child in family/childcare proceedings (art. 4.08)
- Subject is a victim of accident or crime whose next-of-kin have not yet been informed (art. 4.06)
- Subject is in shock or grief and therefore more vulnerable than ordinary sources (art. 3.09)
- Report involves suicide or attempted suicide, where publication of methods could provoke further suicidal actions (art. 4.09)
- Early stage of a criminal investigation, where identification may be premature (art. 4.07)
- Young offender, where identification may cause disproportionate lifelong harm (art. 4.07)

Rationalization cues (illegitimate pressures the code warns against):
- Information is publicly available or already known, suggesting publication is harmless (not an exception the code recognises)
- Subject has made themselves a public figure in an unrelated context (not treated by the code as dissolving privacy protection)
- Competitive pressure to publish identifying details before rivals do (no exception stated; implicitly rejected)

**Cross-linguistic / jurisdictional notes:**
The Norwegian code is notable for using normative imperatives ("Always respect," "Never draw attention to") in Section 4 rather than hedged conditional language. The absoluteness of "Never draw attention to personal or private aspects if they are irrelevant" (art. 4.03) is stronger than comparable universal-norm formulations. The structured exceptions in art. 4.07 (six named justifications for identification in criminal matters) reflect a proportionality tradition consistent with Scandinavian constitutional privacy norms.

**Local-news relevance:**
Not explicitly addressed. However, art. 4.07's heightened caution at early investigation stages and art. 4.08's child-protection rule are especially consequential for local journalism, where subjects and journalists are often personally known to each other and identification carries greater community impact.

**Supporting extracted principles:** #1, #2, #5, #7, #35, #40, #41, #42, #43

tension_name: Editorial independence vs. commercial and advertising pressure
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow commercial relationships — advertising, sponsorship, payment for content, exclusive arrangements — to shape editorial decisions in ways that serve the media organisation's financial interests.
pole_b: Maintain absolute separation between commercial interests and editorial content; ensure all editorial mentions are editorially motivated, all sponsorship is disclosed, and hidden advertising is prohibited in any form.
policy_text: Hidden advertising is incompatible with good press practice.
