pole_b: Before escalating or correcting the record, editors must first seek a response from the accused; procedural fairness requires giving accused parties an opportunity to respond before action is taken against them.
policy_text: Editors should first seek a response from those accused. / The editors should make all reasonable efforts to ensure that a proper investigation is conducted, and if this doesn't happen for whatever reason the editors must persist in obtaining a resolution to the problem and a correction of the record if it is needed.

source_name: COPE Code of Conduct for Editors of Biomedical Journals
tension_name: Substantive independent editorial ethical judgment vs. deference to procedural approval
shared_tension_label: Clear, enforceable ethical rules vs. contextual judgment-based ethics
pole_a: If research has been approved by an ethics committee, that approval constitutes sufficient ethical clearance; the editor need not independently re-evaluate the ethics of the research.
pole_b: Ethics committee approval does not guarantee that research is ethical; editors must independently ensure that published research conforms to internationally accepted ethical guidelines and must not treat procedural approval as a substitute for substantive ethical judgment.
policy_text: The research should where appropriate have been approved by an ethics committee. Editors should recognise that this approval does not guarantee that the research is ethical. / Editors should ensure that research material they publish conforms to internationally accepted ethical guidelines, including, for example, the Declaration of Helsinki.

source_name: COPE Code of Conduct for Editors of Biomedical Journals
tension_name: Openness to critical responses vs. editorial quality gatekeeping
shared_tension_label: Affirmative reciprocal sourcing obligation vs. editorial gatekeeping discretion
pole_a: Editors have a gatekeeping function and may decline to publish critical responses to previously published material when they have convincing reasons for doing so.
pole_b: Cogent critical responses to published material should be published; declining to do so requires convincing reasons, and authors of criticised material should usually be given the opportunity to have a response published.
policy_text: Cogent critical responses to published material should be published unless editors have convincing reasons why they cannot be. / Authors of criticised material should usually be given the opportunity to have a response published.

source_name: COPE Code of Conduct for Editors of Biomedical Journals
tension_name: Accountability and transparency (complaints, advertising) vs. editorial/commercial discretion
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Journals and editors may handle complaints, advertising arrangements, and supplement policies flexibly and informally, without publicly declared procedures, in order to preserve editorial and commercial flexibility.
pole_b: Editors must respond promptly to complaints, ensure dissatisfied complainants have a clear escalation pathway, and maintain declared advertising and supplement policies — all transparency obligations that constrain informal discretion.
policy_text: Editors should respond promptly to complaints and should ensure that there is a way for dissatisfied complainants to take complaints further. Ideally this mechanism should be made clear in the journal. / Editors should have declared policies on advertising in relation to the content of the journal and on processes for publishing supplements.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Truthfulness and verification vs. speed of publication
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish rapidly to meet audience expectations and competitive pressures, accepting that full verification may not be possible in real time.
pole_b: Base all news broadcasting on truthfulness, ensured through appropriate means of verification and proof; never confuse rumour with news.
policy_text: News broadcasting should be based on truthfulness, ensured by the appropriate means of verification and proof, and impartiality in presentation, description and narration. Rumour must not be confused with news.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Editorial/proprietorial authority vs. journalist professional independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Publishers and proprietors may direct editorial content in accordance with their ideological orientations, commercial strategies, and managerial authority over employees.
pole_b: Journalists must be protected from internal pressures; the journalist's freedom of expression is the ultimate safeguard of information, and publishers' ideological orientations are absolutely limited by the requirement of truthful news and ethical opinions.
policy_text: Inside the news organisation, publishers and journalists must co-exist, bearing in mind that the legitimate respect for publishers' and owners' ideological orientations is limited by the absolute requirements on truthful news reporting and ethical opinions. These requirements are such that we must reinforce the safeguards of the journalist's freedom of expression, for they must in the last instance operate as the ultimate sources of information.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Freedom of opinion vs. factual accuracy and non-distortion
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Since opinions are necessarily subjective and cannot be subject to a truthfulness criterion, journalists and commentators have broad latitude to express views without constraint.
pole_b: Opinions must be expressed honestly and ethically, must not deny or conceal the reality of the facts, and must be clearly distinguished from news so that readers cannot confuse the two.
policy_text: Although opinions are necessarily subjective and therefore cannot and should not be made subject to the criterion of truthfulness, we must ensure that opinions are expressed honestly and ethically. / Opinions taking the form of comments on events or actions relating to individuals or institutions should not attempt to deny or conceal the reality of the facts or data.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Privacy of individuals vs. public's right to know
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: The public has a right to information about persons in public life, including their private conduct, and journalism must be able to report it freely.
pole_b: Every individual, including public figures, has the right to respect for private life; intrusion is only justified where a public figure's private conduct demonstrably affects the exercise of their public duties.
policy_text: The right of individuals to privacy must be respected. Persons holding office in public life are entitled to protection for their privacy except in those cases where their private life may have an effect on their public life. The fact that a person holds a public post does not deprive him of the right to respect for his privacy.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Investigative watchdog journalism vs. ethical and legal constraints on methods and framing
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Investigative journalism may require sustained campaigning, undercover methods, and adversarial framing to expose wrongdoing and hold power to account; the importance of the story justifies aggressive means.
pole_b: Investigative journalism is legitimate only within the limits of veracity and honesty; it is incompatible with campaigns based on pre-adopted positions or special interests; information must be gathered by legal and ethical means; the end does not justify the means.
policy_text: In the journalist's profession the end does not justify the means, therefore information must be obtained by legal and ethical means. / Legitimate investigative journalism is limited by the veracity and honesty of information and opinions and is incompatible with journalistic campaigns conducted on the basis of previously adopted positions and special interests.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Commercial/entrepreneurial interests of news organisations vs. information as a citizens' fundamental right
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: News organisations are commercial enterprises that must pursue revenue through audience maximisation, including through content that attracts readers and advertisers, and proprietors have legitimate economic interests to pursue.
pole_b: News organisations are special socio-economic agencies whose entrepreneurial objectives are limited by the conditions for providing access to information as a fundamental right; news must not be exploited for advertising revenue; neither publishers nor journalists own the news.
policy_text: News organisations must consider themselves as special socio-economic agencies whose entrepreneurial objectives have to be limited by the conditions for providing access to a fundamental right. / The media should exploit neither the quality nor the substance of the news or opinions for purposes of boosting readership or audience figures in order to increase advertising revenue.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Journalistic self-regulation and independence vs. external accountability and public oversight
shared_tension_label: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
pole_a: Journalism must be free from external oversight; professional autonomy and editorial independence require that only journalists themselves determine standards and accountability.
pole_b: Self-regulatory bodies comprising diverse stakeholders — publishers, journalists, media users, academics, and judges — must supervise ethical principles; citizens must be empowered to judge journalists' work and credibility; credibility must be publicly measured and published.
policy_text: In order to supervise the implementation of these principles, self-regulatory bodies or mechanisms must be set up comprising publishers, journalists, media-users, associations, experts from the academic world and judges; they will be responsible for issuing resolutions on respect for ethical precepts in journalism, with prior commitment on the part of the media to publish the relevant resolutions.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Confidential source protection vs. transparency and judicial/public demands for disclosure
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Courts, prosecutors, or other authorities may legitimately require journalists to disclose confidential sources in the public interest, particularly in serious criminal matters.
pole_b: Journalists must be legally protected in their right to maintain the confidentiality of sources; the conscience clause and professional secrecy provisions must be legally expanded, clarified, and harmonised across democratic Europe.
policy_text: In this connection we must legally expand and clarify the nature of the conscience clause and professional secrecy vis-à-vis confidential sources, harmonising national provisions on this matter so that they can be implemented in the wider context of democratic Europe.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Presumption of innocence vs. public interest in reporting on ongoing legal proceedings
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: The public has a right to know about ongoing legal proceedings involving public figures or matters of public concern; reporting must not be suppressed merely because a case is sub judice.
pole_b: Journalism must respect the presumption of innocence; in cases that are sub judice, information and opinions must refrain from making judgements.
policy_text: In journalism, information and opinions must respect the presumption of innocence in particular in cases which are still sub judice and must refrain from making judgements.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Right of reply and mandatory correction vs. editorial control and gatekeeping
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Editorial discretion over published content is a core journalistic prerogative; editors determine what is published and when, including whether a correction or reply is warranted.
pole_b: At the request of the persons concerned, the news media must correct automatically and speedily any news item or opinion that is false or erroneous, with all relevant information provided; the right of reply must be implemented and harmonised.
policy_text: At the request of the persons concerned, the news media must correct, automatically and speedily, and with all relevant information provided, any news item or opinion conveyed by them which is false or erroneous. / National legislation should provide for appropriate sanctions and, where applicable, compensation.

source_name: Council of Europe Resolution on the Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Sensationalism and audience appeal vs. substantive public-interest information
shared_tension_label: Audience preference as editorial driver vs. editorial independence from demand
pole_a: Journalists and editors must attract and retain audiences; content that is engaging, dramatic, or emotionally resonant serves the legitimate purpose of keeping citizens informed by maintaining their attention.
pole_b: Journalists must clearly distinguish between controversial or sensational items and subjects on which it is genuinely important to provide information; journalists must not exploit their duties for the purpose of acquiring personal prestige or influence; information must not be exploited to boost readership or advertising revenue.
policy_text: In journalism, controversial or sensational items must not be confused with subjects on which it is important to provide information. / The journalist must not exploit his duties for the principal purpose of acquiring prestige or personal influence.

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Public's right to information vs. protection of private life
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Prioritise the public's entitlement to full, objective information, including details about individuals obtained through surveillance techniques, long-lens photography, or entry onto private property.
pole_b: Respect the reputation and private life of every individual; intrusion is only justified in exceptional cases and solely in the public interest.
policy_text: Intrusions and investigations into the private life of individuals without their consent, including the taking of pictures of people without their knowledge or consent, unless they are involved in events which constitute news of general interest, or on private property and also the gathering of information through bugging devices or long lens photography, are generally unacceptable and their publication can only be justified in exceptional cases and solely in the public interest. (clause 3)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Undercover / deceptive newsgathering vs. honest information-gathering
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use false representation, covert recording, or other deceptive means to obtain information or images when no other route is available and the story is important.
pole_b: Obtain all information and images through honest, legitimate means; do not use false representation, intimidation, blackmail, or take documents without the owner's consent.
policy_text: Functionaries of the Media should not, as a general rule, try to secure information or images/photographs through false representation or any other fraudulent manner. (clause 6); With the exception of serving public interest, documents and images/photographs can only be taken with the consent of their owner. (clause 6)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Presumption of innocence vs. transparent crime and court reporting
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully and immediately on criminal suspects, arrest circumstances, charges, and court appearances — including photographs and identifying details — to inform the public about crime and judicial processes.
pole_b: Fully respect the presumption of innocence; avoid publishing anything that assigns guilt, smears reputation, or publicly humiliates suspects or accused persons; use photographs of uncharged suspects only when professionally necessary.
policy_text: Functionaries of the Media fully respect the principle that a person suspected or accused of having committed a crime is innocent until the contrary is proven in accordance with the law, and consequently avoid publishing anything which may lead to conclusions regarding either the guilt or innocence of suspects or accused or tends to smear their reputation or publicly humiliate them. (clause 9); The Mass Media and media professionals should neither directly nor indirectly assign guilt to the suspect and should avoid any guilt-assigning phrases and characterizations. (guideline 2, item 04)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Suicide reporting suppression vs. public information, transparency, and editorial freedom
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report on suicide cases as newsworthy events — including method, location, identity, and circumstances — in the same way as other deaths, especially when the information was obtained through official or judicial channels.
pole_b: Default to non-publication of suicide news; where exceptional circumstances justify publication, omit method and location details, avoid sensational language, use deterrent framing, account for causal complexity, protect the bereaved, and include help-resource information.
policy_text: No news about suicides is published. In those extraordinary cases that circumstances justify publication, sensitivity and special care should be shown so as to avoid details about the method, even if those details were obtained through a qualified procedure. (clause 5); Where publication is justified, the use of sensational language and expressions or the normalization of suicide or its presentation as a way out of problems must be avoided. (guideline 6); It would be misleading to attribute a suicide to an individual event like exam failure, relationship breakdown or economic catastrophe without delving into other factors. Suicide is never the result of a single cause. (guideline 6)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Sensitivity to harmful/disturbing content vs. the public's right to witness reality
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Publish or broadcast disturbing images and information — violence, death, sexual offences, grief — because the public has a legitimate interest in understanding the full reality of events.
pole_b: Show appropriate sensitivity when presenting issues involving violence, crime, sexual offences, human grief and death; avoid material that could cause panic, horror, or revulsion, especially to children.
policy_text: Show the indicated sensitivity in matters that concern national security and are particularly careful in presenting issues such as violence, crime, sexual offences, human grief and death, as well as information or pictures that are hurtful or could cause panic, horror, or revulsion, especially to children. (General Clauses, item 02); In cases involving mourning, grief or shock, an approach characterised by discretion and sympathy to the utmost degree is necessary, as well as avoidance of any act that may increase human pain. (clause 5)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and market integrity
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Journalists, like any other citizens, may hold personal financial interests (shares, investments) and need not disclose or recuse themselves from covering related topics unless the conflict is flagrant.
pole_b: Declare all personal or family financial interests linked to stories you cover; do not publish investment recommendations in which you have an undisclosed interest; do not trade in shares you are about to report on; maintain an internal register; never use advance economic information for personal benefit; cooperate with the ethics commission.
policy_text: The entanglement of journalists in conflicts of interests is both unacceptable and condemnable. (guideline 5, general principles); Journalists neither publish nor broadcast news regarding investment recommendations if they or their next-of-kin anticipate profit from the selling, holding or otherwise of shares about which they are in possession of information. (guideline 5, §1.2); Functionaries do not make use of, and do not pass on, for their personal benefit, and before being made available to the general public, any information of an economic nature obtained by them. (clause 13)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Freedom of expression (including commentary, satire, and guest speech) vs. dignity and non-discrimination
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Allow journalists, commentators, and broadcast guests broad latitude for sharp criticism, satire, and provocative speech, including language about individuals and groups.
pole_b: Refrain from insulting, abusive, or personal-attack language; do not mock, pillory, or express prejudice based on race, religion, gender, disability, or other protected characteristics; intervene when broadcast guests make xenophobic or prejudiced statements; remove racist online comments immediately.
policy_text: The Media avoid any direct or other reference or action against a person which contains elements of prejudice on the basis of race, colour, language, religion, political or other conviction, national or social origin, property, extraction, gender, age, or other personal status, including physical or mental illness or disability. Scorn, ridicule and abuse of individuals and groups are not permissible. (clause 12); If you are hosting a TV program or a radio program, be prepared to intervene immediately and effectively in order to separate your own position and the position of the Media employing you if your guests, regardless of who they may be, make statements that contain the element of hostility or prejudice against migrants. (guideline 7)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Editorial autonomy in determining newsworthiness vs. equal treatment of migrant-related stories
shared_tension_label: National cultural and linguistic protection vs. critical journalistic independence
pole_a: Journalists and editors exercise independent professional judgment about what is newsworthy; events involving migrants may be more newsworthy precisely because of the public's strong interest in migration as a social phenomenon.
pole_b: Apply the same newsworthiness standard to events involving migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and trafficking victims as to equivalent events involving Cypriots; do not overpublicize stories merely because a victim or perpetrator is a migrant; do not mention national or racial origin unless it is a constitutive or necessary element of the story.
policy_text: Neither write nor report news about events involving migrants, refugees, asylum seekers or human trafficking victims, where such events would not be newsworthy if they involved Cypriots. (guideline 7); Do not declare national or racial origin in news reports when this is not a component of information. For example, if you would not mention that the party or parties involved in a story are Cypriots, opt not to mention it where they are migrants. (guideline 7)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Transparency and identification vs. anonymity protection for vulnerable subjects
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Identify individuals involved in newsworthy events — victims, survivors, asylum seekers, trafficking victims — because full identification serves accuracy, accountability, and the individuals' right to tell their own stories.
pole_b: Never reveal the identity of rape victims, children under 16 in sexual offence cases, asylum seekers, refugees, and trafficking victims; protect the anonymity of hospital patients and accident victims; apply special care to any content that could enable indirect identification.
policy_text: The Media do not reveal, either directly or indirectly, the identity of victims of rape or other sexual offences. (clause 10); The identity of children under 16 who are complainants, witnesses or accused in cases of sexual offences is never revealed. (clause 10, item 01); Never reveal the identity of asylum seekers, refugees, victims of human trafficking, even migrants who choose to speak on camera because either they or their relatives may face retaliation by the authorities of their country of origin or by non-State, even criminal organizations. (guideline 7)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Collegial respect vs. public accountability of fellow journalists
shared_tension_label: Professional solidarity vs. accountability for unethical colleagues
pole_a: Hold colleagues publicly and critically accountable for professional errors, ethical violations, and inaccurate reporting, using pointed criticism where warranted in the public interest.
pole_b: Comment on colleagues' work with due respect for their honour and reputation; refrain from personal attacks and from language that belittles a colleague's personality.
policy_text: Journalists, in commenting on the work of their colleagues do so with due respect to their honour and reputation and refrain from personal attacks and references belittling the personality. (General Clauses)

source_name: Cyprus Journalists' Code of Practice (including General Clauses, Special Clauses, and Addendum – Explanatory Guidelines)
tension_name: Right of reply vs. editorial control and legal self-protection
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Exercise full editorial discretion over published replies, including refusing letters that may have legal repercussions; edit replies substantially to meet space or content constraints.
pole_b: Give a fair, timely, and substantively unimpaired opportunity of reply to those affected — especially those who have been attacked — publishing the reply close enough to the original coverage that it remains meaningful; limit editing to length without altering substance.
policy_text: The Media give a fair opportunity of reply, in the appropriate case, to those affected and particularly when they have been attacked. This opportunity will be given not so long after the time of publication, that the right of reply shall have no meaning. (clause 2); Media may edit long letters provided the substance of the reply is not affected. Media may refuse to publish letters that may have legal repercussions on the Media or third parties. (clause 2, conditions)

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Truth-telling vs. source protection
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Disclose confidential source information when doing so serves the full truth and the public's right to know.
pole_b: Keep professional secrecy and never disclose a source obtained in confidence, even when doing so means that some truth remains unpublished or unattributed.
policy_text: Keep professional secrecy and do not disclose the source of information obtained in confidence (duty 7), set against Respect the truth, whatever the consequences for oneself, because of the public's right to know the truth (duty 1).

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Verification before publication vs. urgency of public information
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish available information promptly to serve the public's right to know, even if origin or accuracy cannot yet be fully verified.
pole_b: Publish only information whose origin is known; if origin is uncertain, accompany the information with explicit reservations. Never make unfounded accusations.
policy_text: Publish only information whose origin is known, or accompany it with the required reservations if necessary (duty 3), and forbid unfounded accusations (duty 8).

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Categorical prohibition on disloyal methods vs. investigative public interest
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use covert, deceptive, or otherwise "disloyal" methods to gather information when the story serves a compelling public interest that cannot be exposed by other means.
pole_b: Never use disloyal or deceptive methods to obtain information, photographs, or documents, regardless of the public-interest value of the story.
policy_text: Do not use disloyal methods to obtain information, photographs, and documents. (duty 4)

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Freedom of commentary and criticism vs. prohibition on defamation and unfounded accusations
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Publish robust, pointed critical commentary or allegations about public figures and institutions, even at the risk of the content being characterised as defamatory or not fully proved.
pole_b: Ensure that all critical commentary is grounded in verifiable facts; forbid slander, defamation, and unfounded accusations regardless of how important the underlying public-interest case may seem.
policy_text: Defend freedom of information, commentary, and criticism (duty 2), but forbid oneself … slander, defamation, unfounded accusations (duty 8).

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Economic dependence on advertisers vs. editorial independence from commercial interests
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accommodate advertiser interests — directly or indirectly — in editorial decisions about what to publish or suppress, in exchange for financial support that sustains the outlet.
pole_b: Maintain complete editorial independence from advertisers; never confuse journalism with advertising or propaganda; refuse any advantage offered in exchange for publishing or suppressing information; ensure economic independence through adequate remuneration.
policy_text: Never confuse the journalist's profession with that of the advertiser or propagandist; accept no directive, direct or indirect, from advertisers (duty 9); prohibit receiving any advantage in return for the publication or suppression of information (duty 8); journalists are entitled to remuneration … sufficient to guarantee their economic independence (right 5).

source_name: Déclaration de Munich (1971) — Déclaration des devoirs et des droits des journalistes
tension_name: Managerial prerogative over organisational decisions vs. editorial team participation rights
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Allow management to make all significant organisational decisions — including staffing, restructuring, and editorial direction — unilaterally as an expression of ownership and managerial authority.
pole_b: Mandate that the editorial team be informed of all important decisions affecting the organisation's life, and be consulted — before any final decision — on all matters relating to the composition of the editorial team.
policy_text: The editorial team must be mandatorily informed of any important decision likely to affect the life of the organisation. It must be at least consulted, before any final decision, on any measure relating to the composition of the editorial team: hiring, dismissal, reassignment, and promotion of journalists. (right 4)

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Truth-seeking vs. privacy protection
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Publish all truthful, relevant information about individuals regardless of whether it intrudes on private life, because the public has a right to know.
pole_b: Respect individuals' private lives and suppress or withhold privately damaging information unless the public interest specifically requires disclosure.
policy_text: Respect the private lives of individuals, insofar as the public interest does not require otherwise.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Truth-seeking vs. human dignity in reporting atrocities and sensitive categories
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report fully and graphically on war, terrorism, disasters, and individuals' sensitive personal characteristics (ethnicity, religion, sex, disability) because complete, unvarnished truth serves the public's right to know.
pole_b: Limit reporting on atrocities by the respect owed to victims' suffering and relatives' feelings; avoid any discriminatory allusion to personal characteristics in text, image, or sound.
policy_text: The reporting, through text, image and sound, of war, terrorist acts, accidents and disasters finds its limits in the respect owed to the suffering of victims and the feelings of their relatives.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. transparency and completeness of information
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Fully disclose the identity and nature of sources so the public can assess the reliability of information and essential facts are not suppressed.
pole_b: Never reveal a confidential source under any circumstances; treat source identity as absolutely protected.
policy_text: Not to reveal the sources of information obtained in confidence.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Verification / known-origin requirement vs. speed of disclosure and completeness
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish information quickly and completely to serve the public's right to know, even when origin is uncertain or confirmation is pending.
pole_b: Publish only information whose origin is known, and label unconfirmed information explicitly as such; do not suppress essential information, but do not present unverified material as fact.
policy_text: Publish only information, documents, images, and sounds whose origin is known to him/her. … To identify very precisely as such news that is unconfirmed.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Prohibition on disloyal methods vs. truth-seeking through investigative journalism
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever methods — including undercover work, deception, or other "disloyal" techniques — that are necessary to uncover truth in the public interest.
pole_b: Obtain information only by fair and loyal methods; never use deceptive or disloyal techniques regardless of the public interest served.
policy_text: Not to use disloyal methods to obtain information, sounds, images, or documents.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Public accountability primacy vs. legitimate editorial authority
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Follow the directives of your designated editorial managers and the editorial line of your outlet as the primary framework governing your journalistic conduct.
pole_b: Give absolute priority to your responsibility toward the public; reject any editorial directive — even from designated managers — that conflicts with that responsibility or with this declaration.
policy_text: Journalists' responsibility toward the public must take precedence over those they assume toward third parties, including public authorities and employers. … Not to accept journalistic directives other than from the designated managers of one's newsroom, and only insofar as those directives are not contrary to the present declaration.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Editorial and advertising independence vs. commercial and economic pressures
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept financial benefits, advertiser preferences, or commercially motivated editorial adjustments as a practical accommodation to the economic realities of running a media outlet.
pole_b: Reject all advantages, advertiser instructions, and commercial influences on editorial content; maintain complete separation between journalistic work and advertising or public relations.
policy_text: Not to accept any advantage or any promise that could limit their professional independence or the expression of their own opinion. … To forbid oneself from confusing the profession of journalist with that of advertiser. … Not to accept any instruction, direct or indirect, from advertising clients.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Freedom of commentary and criticism vs. anti-discrimination and dignity duties
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Exercise unrestricted freedom of commentary and criticism, including commentary that involves characterising individuals by personal attributes such as religion, ethnicity, or other identity categories.
pole_b: Refrain from any commentary or criticism that involves discriminatory allusions to personal characteristics (ethnicity, nationality, religion, sex, sexual orientation, illness, disability), and conduct all commentary within the limits set by respect for human dignity.
policy_text: Defend freedom of information and the rights it implies, freedom of commentary and criticism, the independence and dignity of the profession. … The journalist must avoid any allusion, through text, image or sound, to a person's ethnic or national belonging, to their religion … that would have a discriminatory character.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Conscience-based refusal vs. acceptance of editorial directives
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Follow editorial directives from designated managers as a general professional obligation, even when the journalist has personal reservations about the assignment.
pole_b: Refuse any professional act or opinion that violates the rules of the profession or the journalist's own conscience, and claim the right to do so without suffering any penalty.
policy_text: The right for the journalist not to perform any professional act — and in particular not to express any opinion — contrary to the rules of his/her profession or to his/her conscience; he/she must not suffer any prejudice as a result of his/her refusal.

source_name: Déclaration des devoirs et des droits du/de la Journaliste
tension_name: Self-regulation and rejection of state interference vs. legal accountability and public accountability
shared_tension_label: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
pole_a: Submit professional journalistic conduct to external oversight — state regulation, courts, or other external bodies — as a mechanism for ensuring genuine accountability to the public served.
pole_b: Journalists self-regulate through peer bodies (Press Council or equivalent); reject all state or external interference in professional ethical matters, while remaining subject to the common law of each country.
policy_text: Journalists spontaneously impose on themselves the rules necessary for the accomplishment of their information mission. … In professional matters he/she accepts no jurisdiction other than that of his/her peers, the Press Council, or any analogous body legitimised to rule on professional ethical questions. He/she rejects all interference, state or otherwise, in this domain.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Speed vs. accuracy — digital immediacy vs. due-diligence verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish rapidly to meet competitive digital-media expectations, even if full verification has not been completed.
pole_b: Verify all information with due diligence and resort to reliable sources before publication, treating immediacy as no excuse for omitting deontological principles.
policy_text: As in other media, the immediacy is no excuse to omit deontological principles as resorting to reliable sources and verifying the information. / disclose only information that's been verified with due diligence and avoid spreading conjectures and rumours as if they were facts.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Truth and public interest vs. dignity and harm avoidance
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Prioritise the completeness and accuracy of published information even when it causes harm to individuals' dignity, reputation, or emotional wellbeing.
pole_b: Avoid disclosing imprecise or insufficiently based facts that injure dignity or cause harm; contact affected parties before publication; treat vulnerable people with special care; restrict reporting of suicides; avoid posthumous dignity harm.
policy_text: The journalists should not use abusive expressions nor disclose facts that are imprecise or without sufficient basis and that may injure the dignity of people and cause harm or discredit to public or private entities. / People should be treated with respect and dignity, particularly the most vulnerable ones. / The cases of suicide will be disclosed only when they have personal relevance or a real public interest, bearing in mind always the risk of a mimetic effect.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Source transparency vs. source protection
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Withhold source identities from readers to protect confidential informants, even at the cost of reducing the verifiability and credibility of published information.
pole_b: Cite sources to assure the credibility of information and enable readers to evaluate its basis.
policy_text: To assure the credibility of the information, the sources must be quoted. / journalists have the moral obligation to protect them by invoking professional secrecy when necessary. Confidentiality is useful to protect people in a situation of vulnerability or risk, but in no case the anonymity can be used for unjustified attacks against individuals and organizations.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Investigative necessity vs. prohibition on surreptitious newsgathering methods
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use hidden cameras, surreptitious procedures, or interception of private communications to obtain information of genuine public importance that cannot be obtained otherwise.
pole_b: Use only legitimate and transparent methods to obtain information; surreptitious and misleading procedures are unacceptable as a default.
policy_text: The use of hidden cameras and any other surreptitious or misleading procedure to obtain information, pictures and testimonies is unacceptable. / The interception and revelation without consent of private material obtained from mobile telephones, electronic messaging and other communication devices is also unacceptable.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Public's right to know about alleged crimes vs. presumption of innocence
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully and immediately on police investigations, criminal charges and alleged crimes as matters of public concern, identifying suspects and describing the alleged offences in detail.
pole_b: Protect the presumption of innocence throughout all reporting from the start of police intervention until guilt is legally proved; prevent prejudice; avoid submitting suspects to parallel trials.
policy_text: Any person accused of or charged for a crime has the right to the presumption of innocence in the information and opinions related to the investigations, lawsuits or criminal proceedings. The respect and protection of this right is valid from the beginning of the police interventions until guilt has been proved in a process celebrated with the necessary guarantees. / The journalists should prevent prejudices and should not submit suspects to parallel trials.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Archival integrity and collective memory vs. individual right to online erasure
shared_tension_label: Permanent Public Record vs. Right to Be Forgotten (Digital)
pole_a: Honour individual requests to delete or suppress online documents and data traces, including for reasons of personal image, changed opinions, or reputational rehabilitation.
pole_b: Preserve the online archive as collective heritage and living memory; resist erasure demands based solely on personal preference, change of opinion or image; while ensuring persistence does not cause abusive fundamental-rights harm.
policy_text: the invocation of the right to oblivion should not be reason for the immediate destruction of items that in some ways are part of a general archive or living memory which is a collective heritage and eventually may be of interest to historians and social researchers. / However, the persistence of certain documents should not generate abusive or harmful situations at the expense of the fundamental rights of the person.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Editorial independence vs. commercial and financial entanglements
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept payments, gifts, or secondary paid activities from third parties in ways that may influence or appear to influence journalistic output, justifying them as economically necessary or commercially normal.
pole_b: Maintain complete independence by refusing third-party payments, keeping gifts within strict courtesy limits, avoiding simultaneous paid activities that endanger truthfulness, refusing disguised advertising, and avoiding all conflicts of interest — political, commercial, financial, or familial.
policy_text: The journalists should never accept payments or rewards by third parties that intend to promote, orient or get published certain information and opinions. / It is not admissible to practise journalism simultaneously with other paid activities that endanger the principles of truthfulness and independence. / As a general rule, the information professionals should avoid any situation of conflict of interests, whether political, commercial, economic, financial or familiar, that calls into question the credibility and impartiality of his role.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Non-discriminatory and dignified language vs. accurate factual reporting
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Use precise legal or factual terminology in reporting — including terms like "illegal" for persons in irregular migration status, or nationality/ethnicity in crime reporting — in the interest of accuracy and reader clarity.
pole_b: Choose language that affirms dignity, avoids criminalising labels for entire groups, and prevents discriminatory stereotyping, even when this requires departing from common legal or colloquial terminology.
policy_text: People can never be illegal because this would deny to a human being the category of subject of law. / The use of this word to designate, exclusively and continuously, the collective of workers who migrate means a discriminatory treatment and promotes stereotypes that criminalize the image of these people in the collective consciousness. / the journalists should avoid in any case the generalizations and the labelling of people because of differential features, whether ethnic, religious, economic or social.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Protection of minors vs. public's right to know
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Report fully on matters involving children when those children are central to stories of significant public interest, using their identity and image where this adds essential clarity or newsworthiness.
pole_b: Protect minors' identities as victims, witnesses or suspects; require explicit parental/guardian consent before interviewing, photographing or filming children; refuse to use a relative's public prominence as justification for exploiting a child's image.
policy_text: Spreading the identity of minors should be avoided when they appear as victims (except in the case of murder and cases of kidnappings or disappearances), witnesses or suspects. / As a general rule, children should not be interviewed nor photographed or filmed without the explicit consent of their parents, legal guardians, teachers or educators. / It is also not fair to allege the public relevance of relatives or close people to justify the interference in the children's private life or the exploitation of their image.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Open online expression and user participation vs. publisher responsibility to moderate
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Allow open, unmoderated user comments and contributions on news websites as an expression of free speech and democratic participation, without imposing registration or censorship.
pole_b: Require prior registration for online commenters; moderate user feedback to prevent offensive, dignity-violating, discriminatory, or hate-inciting content; treat online contributions with the same responsibility as letters to the editor.
policy_text: Feedback from users to the news disclosed on informative websites should be moderated by responsible publishers. These should count with mechanisms and appropriate tools to prevent the dissemination of offensive messages which could violate the dignity of the people and social groups or stimulate discrimination, violence and hatred. / The contributions on the Internet should not be anonymous. The diffuser should require a prior registration for users who wish to comment and give their opinions, in the same way that newspapers don't publish letters to the editor written by people who have not been properly identified.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Peace journalism values vs. conventional news values in conflict reporting
shared_tension_label: Honest reporting on armed conflict vs. rejection of war propaganda
pole_a: Follow conventional news values in conflict reporting: prioritise dramatic events, active violence, leaders and official processes, and abandon coverage once a ceasefire is reached.
pole_b: Adopt a peace journalism orientation: give voice to all parties, humanise all sides, avoid faction language, highlight grassroots peace efforts, report causes and invisible effects of violence, cover pre-violence tensions and post-conflict reconstruction, avoid sensationalism, and cite sources transparently even for confronted factions.
policy_text: Give voice to all actors and promote the understanding between the parties involved. Dialogue must be encouraged. / Do not dehumanize one of the parts; it is necessary to report about the victims as well as the attackers. / Avoid the language of the warring factions and their allies. / Do not abandon the coverage after the cease-of-fire and deal with the resolution, reconstruction and reconciliation. / Report on a conflict even if there is no violence, because that can help to prevent it.

source_name: Declaration of Principles of Professional Journalists (Catalonia)
tension_name: Right to information vs. right not to provide information / prohibition on harassment
shared_tension_label: Investigative Persistence vs. Harassment and Desist Compliance
pole_a: Pursue information aggressively and persistently from all sources, including those who refuse to respond, in the public interest and in defence of transparency.
pole_b: Concede to individuals and legal persons the right not to answer questions; treat intimidating or persistent harassment as reprehensible; while separately defending the right to information against unjustified institutional restrictions.
policy_text: The journalist must defend the right to information in front of any restriction to the transparency required by the public interest, especially when the sources are government institutions and agencies. / one must concede the individual and legal persons the right not to provide any information or to answer questions. Intimidating and persistent harassment is a reprehensible practice.

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Fair newsgathering methods vs. public-interest investigation
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use any method necessary — including undercover reporting, deception, or other ethically contested techniques — to obtain information of significant public importance.
pole_b: Use only fair and ethical methods to obtain news, photographs, or documents — with no exception for public-interest stories.
policy_text: Not to use unfair methods to obtain news, photographs or documents

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Employer/editorial loyalty vs. overriding public responsibility
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Subordinate journalistic decisions to the interests and instructions of employers, public authorities, or the information organ's commercial requirements.
pole_b: Recognise that responsibility to the public exceeds all other responsibilities, including those owed to employers and public authorities.
policy_text: The journalist's responsibility towards the public excels any other responsibility, particularly towards employers and public authorities.

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Vigorous criticism vs. prohibition on defamatory falsehoods
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Publish aggressive, contested characterisations of persons or institutions — including accusations that may prove unfounded — in the name of free expression and the public's right to know.
pole_b: Ensure all accusations and characterisations are factually grounded; treat calumny, slander, libel, and unfounded accusations as grave professional offences.
policy_text: To regard as grave professional offences the following: plagiarism, calumny, slander, libel and unfounded accusations / To defend freedom of information, comment and criticism

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Economic security vs. independence from commercial and corrupt pressure
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Allow financial dependence on employers, advertisers, or other paymasters to shape editorial decisions, either by suppressing unfavourable stories or publishing favourable ones in exchange for economic benefit.
pole_b: Maintain full editorial independence by refusing bribery in any form, refusing advertiser orders, and securing individual contracts that guarantee material and moral security.
policy_text: the acceptance of bribe in any form in consideration of either publication or suppression of news / Never to confuse the profession of a journalist with that of advertisements salesman or a propagandist and to refuse any direct or indirect orders from advertisers / guaranteeing his economic independence

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Peer self-regulation vs. subjection to general national law
shared_tension_label: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
pole_a: Allow governments or other external bodies to assert jurisdiction over professional journalistic conduct, treating journalism as an ordinary regulated activity.
pole_b: Recognise that in professional matters, only journalistic peers have jurisdiction; exclude all government interference in the assessment and regulation of professional conduct.
policy_text: Within the general law of each country, the journalist recognises, in professional matters, the jurisdiction of his colleagues only; he excludes every kind of interference by governments or others.

source_name: Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Journalists (IFJ Munich Declaration, 1971)
tension_name: Editorial staff participation vs. managerial authority over enterprise decisions
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Allow media enterprise management to make unilateral decisions about staffing, editorial composition, and enterprise direction without editorial staff input.
pole_b: Ensure editorial staff are informed of all important enterprise decisions and are at minimum consulted before final decisions on recruitment, dismissals, mutations, and promotions.
policy_text: The editorial staff has obligatorily to be informed on all important decisions which may influence the life of the enterprise. It should at least be consulted before a definitive decision on all matters related to the composition of the editorial staff e.g. recruitment, dismissals, mutations and promotion of journalists is taken.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Speed vs. Accuracy
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish information promptly, accepting that some errors may later require correction.
pole_b: Verify information as thoroughly as possible before publication, even if this delays the story.
policy_text: It is the duty of the media to publish information correctly and promptly. As far as possible it should be verified whether the information given or reproduced is correct.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Transparency (Right of Reply) vs. Subject Protection and Source Security
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish potentially prejudicial information without approaching the subject, especially when contact could delay publication, expose a source, or forewarn a wrongdoer.
pole_b: Before publishing information that may be prejudicial, insulting, or damaging, submit the material to the person concerned and allow reasonable time for a response; publish attacks and replies together wherever possible.
policy_text: Information which may be prejudicial or insulting or detract from the respect in which individuals should be held shall be very closely examined before publication, primarily by submission to the person concerned. Submission should be made so as to give the person concerned a reasonable time to reply.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Editorial/Narrative Voice vs. Fact–Comment Separation
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Blend factual reporting with interpretation, analysis, and editorial voice in a single piece, making journalistic judgement visible within the narrative.
pole_b: Draw a clear distinction between factual information and editorial comment so that audiences can always tell which is which; ensure headlines accurately reflect, and are substantiated by, the article content.
policy_text: A clear distinction shall be drawn between factual information and comments. / The form and content of headlines and subheadlines shall be substantiated by the article or publication in question.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Harm Minimisation vs. Duty to Inform (Vulnerable Subjects)
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Treat coverage of suicide, accident victims, crime victims, witnesses, and vulnerable persons (including children) as fully newsworthy, publishing whatever is accurate and in the public interest without special restraint.
pole_b: Apply the greatest possible consideration and tact to coverage involving suicide, accident and crime victims, witnesses, relatives, and vulnerable persons; obtain parental consent for child interviews where indicated; do not exploit vulnerability in gathering information.
policy_text: Suicides or attempted suicides should not be mentioned unless an obvious public interest requires or justifies public coverage, and in that case the coverage should be as considerate as possible. / Victims of crimes or accidents shall be paid the greatest possible regard. / Special regard should be paid to children and other persons who cannot be expected to realise the effects of their statements or other involvement.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Investigative Necessity vs. Privacy and Consent (Clandestine Methods)
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use clandestine recordings or exploit a source's vulnerability when necessary to expose wrongdoing of public importance, accepting that privacy interests must sometimes yield to investigative need.
pole_b: Publish clandestine recordings only with the consent of those recorded, or when societal interest clearly overrides individual privacy AND no other means of obtaining the evidence is available; never exploit confidence, feelings, or lack of experience to gather information.
policy_text: Clandestine recordings should only be published if the persons involved have given their consent, or if the interests of society clearly supersede the claim for protection of the individual and it is not possible, or only possible with great difficulty, to obtain the necessary journalistic evidence in any other way.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Presumption of Innocence vs. Transparency in Legal Proceedings
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully and transparently on criminal investigations and proceedings, including naming suspects, publishing police complaints, and characterising the strength of the case — treating the justice system as a matter of legitimate public scrutiny at every stage.
pole_b: Withhold or restrain publication of information that could prejudice a case or imply guilt before a final decision; apply caution in naming suspects and persons against whom police complaints have been laid; follow cases through to their conclusion; ensure equal representation of prosecution and defence.
policy_text: As long as a criminal case has not been finally decided or the charge withdrawn, no information may be published which may obstruct the clearing up of the case, nor may pronouncements to the effect that a suspect or accused is guilty be published.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Contextual Completeness vs. Non-Stigmatisation (Personal Characteristics and Prior Convictions)
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Report all available contextual information about a person — including ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, prior criminal record — to give audiences a full picture of who is involved and the broader patterns the case may reflect.
pole_b: Include personal characteristics (race, ethnicity, nationality, creed, sexual orientation, family circumstances, organisational membership) only when directly relevant to the case; spare persons from having irrelevant prior convictions highlighted.
policy_text: Family circumstances, race, ethnicity, nationality, creed, sexual orientation or membership of organisations should only be mentioned when relevant to the case. / A suspect, an accused, or a convicted person should be spared from having attention called to an earlier conviction if it is without importance in relation to the offence concerning which he/she is now suspected, charged, or convicted.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Commercial Viability vs. Editorial Independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept advertising content, commercially driven material, or outside editorial influence when necessary for the financial survival of the outlet, provided audiences are broadly aware that commercial pressures exist.
pole_b: Maintain a strict separation between advertising and editorial content; publish commercially generated material only when a clear journalistic criterion independently justifies it; refuse outside demands for influence over editorial content that could raise doubts about the medium's independence.
policy_text: A clear distinction shall be drawn between advertising and editorial content. Text, sound and images generated by direct or indirect commercial interests should be published only if a clear journalistic criterion calls for publication. / Breach of sound press ethics also includes… compliance with outsiders' demands for influence over the content of the media, if such compliance may raise doubt as to the freedom and independence of the media.

source_name: Denmark Press Ethical Rules (Pressenævnet / Danish Press Council)
tension_name: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience Clause
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Editors and publishers retain full authority to assign stories, determine editorial approach, and require journalists to produce content that serves the outlet's editorial line — including content the individual journalist finds objectionable.
pole_b: Journalists must not be assigned tasks that conflict with the press ethical rules, and should not be assigned tasks contrary to their personal conscience or convictions.
policy_text: Furthermore, a breach of sound press ethics exists if tasks that are in conflict with the present press ethical rules are imposed on a journalist. Journalists should not have tasks imposed on them that are contrary to their conscience or convictions.

source_name: East Africa Free Press Assembly Code of Ethics
tension_name: Completeness and right of reply vs. timeliness of accurate publication
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish accurate information as soon as it is verified, without waiting for all sides to respond or for a right-of-reply process to be completed.
pole_b: Before publishing, report all sides of the story and obtain a right of reply from any person mentioned unfavourably; cross-check facts through adequate enquiry.
policy_text: All sides of the story shall be reported. / The right to reply from any person mentioned in an unfavourable context shall be obtained, as appropriate. / the journalist's duty to make adequate enquiries and cross check his/her facts.

source_name: East Africa Free Press Assembly Code of Ethics
tension_name: Avoiding discriminatory/stigmatising language vs. accurate and complete reporting
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Report identity characteristics (nationality, ethnicity, religion, sex, disability, etc.) when they are factually relevant to the story, even if doing so risks stigmatising language or effects.
pole_b: Avoid prejudiced, pejorative, or stigmatising language in reference to a person's identity characteristics; include such references only when directly and demonstrably relevant to the story's substance.
policy_text: The mass media shall avoid prejudiced, pejorative or stigmatising language in reference to, among other things, a person's nationality, ethnicity, class, religion, political affiliation or sex, or to any physical or mental illness or disability. / Such references shall be eschewed unless they are germane to a story.

source_name: East Africa Free Press Assembly Code of Ethics
tension_name: Absolute prohibition on inducements vs. operational realities of under-resourced journalism
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept gifts, free travel, or other forms of practical support from sources or interested parties when no alternative means of covering a story exists — particularly where media organisations cannot fund coverage independently.
pole_b: Refuse all gifts, bribes, favours, free travel, special treatment, and any other form of inducement or privilege that could create a real or apparent conflict of interest; journalists and their employers must conduct themselves to protect against such conflicts.
policy_text: Journalists and their employers shall conduct themselves in a manner that protects them from real or apparent conflicts of interest. / Such conflicts of interest may arise through accepting gifts, bribes, favours, free travel, special treatment or any other form of inducement or privilege.

source_name: East and Central African Code of Ethics
tension_name: Speed vs. verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish promptly, accepting that full cross-checking of every fact may be deferred or incomplete under deadline or competitive pressure.
pole_b: Make adequate enquiries and cross-check all facts before publishing; recognise that accuracy is a public right, not merely a professional preference.
policy_text: It is the public's right to unbiased, accurate, balanced and comprehensive information, and the journalist's duty to make adequate enquiries and cross check his/her facts.

source_name: East and Central African Code of Ethics
tension_name: Right of reply vs. timeliness / editorial feasibility
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish a story that mentions a person unfavourably without first obtaining their response, when circumstances make doing so impractical or unduly slow.
pole_b: Seek and obtain the right of reply from any person mentioned unfavourably before publishing; treat this as a near-absolute obligation that protects both fairness and the subject's dignity.
policy_text: The right to reply from any person mentioned in an unfavourable context shall be obtained, as appropriate.

source_name: East and Central African Code of Ethics
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. accuracy and attribution
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Credit sources fully and publicly, and enable the public to evaluate the reliability of information by disclosing who provided it — even when sources would prefer confidentiality.
pole_b: Maintain absolute professional secrecy regarding the identity of confidential sources; the obligation to protect sources is unconditional and overrides full attribution.
policy_text: The journalist shall observe professional secrecy regarding the source of information obtained in confidence. / It is the duty of the journalist to regard plagiarism as unethical and to always credit the source.

source_name: East and Central African Code of Ethics
tension_name: Avoiding discriminatory language vs. reporting accurate, relevant context
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Include references to a person's nationality, ethnicity, religion, class, sex, disability, or similar characteristics as background context, even when their direct relevance to the story is debatable.
pole_b: Omit all prejudiced, pejorative, or stigmatising identity references unless they are directly germane to the story being reported.
policy_text: The mass media shall avoid prejudiced, pejorative or stigmatising language in reference to, among other things, a person's nationality, ethnicity, class, religion, political affiliation or sex, or to any physical or mental illness or disability. / Such references shall be eschewed unless they are germane to a story.

source_name: East and Central African Code of Ethics
tension_name: Conflict-of-interest avoidance vs. source-relationship building
shared_tension_label: Financial self-interest vs. journalistic independence and credibility
pole_a: Accept modest gifts, hospitality, or favours from sources as part of normal relationship-building that facilitates access and information-gathering — particularly in resource-constrained environments where such norms are culturally expected.
pole_b: Refuse all gifts, bribes, favours, free travel, special treatment, and other inducements from any source or interested party, regardless of value or intent, in order to protect against real or apparent conflicts of interest.
policy_text: Journalists and their employers shall conduct themselves in a manner that protects them from real or apparent conflicts of interest. Such conflicts of interest may arise through accepting gifts, bribes, favours, free travel, special treatment or any other form of inducement or privilege.

source_name: Empowering Children in the Media: Editorial Guidelines for Reporting on Children
tension_name: Truth-seeking vs. minimising harm to children
shared_tension_label: Truth-seeking vs. minimising harm to children
pole_a: Publish accurate and full information about children and situations affecting them, including identifying details, images, and sensitive facts, in service of truth-seeking and public understanding.
pole_b: Withhold, obscure, or limit information about children whenever publication would cause harm, trauma, distress, humiliation, embarrassment, grief, or danger to the child, even at the cost of completeness.
policy_text: Seek the truth and report it accurately and as fully as possible. / Minimise harm. / Always respect children's dignity and well-being. The dignity and rights of every child are to be respected in every circumstance. / Where a child's circumstances makes him/her especially vulnerable… journalists must demonstrate extreme care to ensure their reporting does not cause further harm, trauma, distress, humiliation, embarrassment, grief or expose them to danger.
