Disclose unavoidable conflicts. / Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment. / Deny favored treatment to advertisers, donors or any other special interests, and resist internal and external pressure to influence coverage. / Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two. Prominently label sponsored content.

source_name: Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics (2014)
tension_name: Prompt, Prominent Correction vs. Reputational and Legal Self-Interest
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Delay, minimise, or bury corrections to protect the outlet's reputation and reduce legal exposure.
pole_b: Acknowledge errors promptly and correct them prominently and clearly; explain corrections so audiences understand what was wrong and what is now right; respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity, and fairness.
policy_text: Acknowledge mistakes and correct them promptly and prominently. Explain corrections and clarifications carefully and clearly. / Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness.

source_name: Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics (2014)
tension_name: Exposing Internal Wrongdoing vs. Institutional Loyalty
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Protect the organisation from internal exposure by overlooking or silently tolerating ethical violations by colleagues or employers.
pole_b: Apply the watchdog obligation inward as well as outward; expose unethical conduct within journalism including within your own organisation; hold yourself to the same standards you expect of others.
policy_text: Expose unethical conduct in journalism, including within their organizations. / Abide by the same high standards they expect of others.

source_name: Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics (2014)
tension_name: Newsworthiness of Graphic / Disturbing Content vs. Avoiding Sensationalism
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Publish or broadcast graphic, disturbing, or lurid material because audiences are drawn to it and it may be genuinely newsworthy.
pole_b: Exercise editorial restraint; avoid pandering to morbid or lurid curiosity even when competitors are publishing such content; assess whether disturbing content is genuinely required to serve the public interest or merely satisfies prurient audience demand.
policy_text: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity, even if others do. / Balance the public's need for information against potential harm or discomfort.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Speed vs. Verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly to meet timeliness demands, accepting that some information may be unverified or incomplete at the moment of publication.
pole_b: Base all news broadcasting on truthfulness, ensured by appropriate means of verification and proof before publication; never confuse rumour with news.
policy_text: News broadcasting should be based on truthfulness, ensured by the appropriate means of verification and proof, and impartiality in presentation, description and narration. / Rumour must not be confused with news.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: News–Opinion Distinction vs. Editorial Voice and Opinion Leadership
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Allow journalists and media organisations to express strong editorial opinions, take positions on public affairs, and lead audiences toward particular interpretations of events, blurring the line between reporting and commentary.
pole_b: Draw a clear, visible distinction between news (factual information) and opinion (thoughts, beliefs, value judgements); ensure audiences cannot confuse them; express opinions honestly but never use them to deny or conceal factual reality or to create or shape public opinion.
policy_text: The basic principle of any ethical consideration of journalism is that a clear distinction must be drawn between news and opinions, making it impossible to confuse them. / Opinions taking the form of comments on events or actions relating to individuals or institutions should not attempt to deny or conceal the reality of the facts or data.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Freedom of Expression / Public Right to Know vs. Individual Privacy
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Prioritise the public's right to information and freedom of expression, publishing information about individuals — including public figures — without considering their right to private life.
pole_b: Respect every individual's right to privacy; in cases involving persons in public life, maintain privacy protection except where their private life has a demonstrable effect on their public role; seek a balance between Article 8 ECHR (privacy) and Article 10 ECHR (expression).
policy_text: The right of individuals to privacy must be respected. Persons holding office in public life are entitled to protection for their privacy except in those cases where their private life may have an effect on their public life. / The attempt to strike a balance between the right to respect for private life, enshrined in Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, and the freedom of expression set forth in Article 10, is well documented in the recent case-law of the European Commission and Court of Human Rights.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Investigative / Watchdog Journalism vs. Presumption of Innocence
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report aggressively on alleged wrongdoing by individuals and institutions, naming suspects and drawing conclusions about guilt before or during legal proceedings.
pole_b: Ensure all information and opinions respect the presumption of innocence; refrain from making judgements about individuals, particularly in cases still sub judice; conduct investigative journalism only within the bounds of veracity and honesty, not on the basis of pre-adopted positions or special interests.
policy_text: In journalism, information and opinions must respect the presumption of innocence, in particular in cases which are still sub judice, and must refrain from making judgments. / legitimate investigative journalism is limited by the veracity and honesty of information and opinions and is incompatible with journalistic campaigns conducted on the basis of previously adopted positions and special interests.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Commercial Media Imperatives vs. Public-Interest Information Duty
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Allow commercial logic — audience maximisation, advertising revenue, competitive advantage, sensationalism — to drive editorial decisions about what to publish and how to present it.
pole_b: Treat information as a fundamental right of citizens, not a commodity; limit entrepreneurial objectives of news organisations by the duty to provide access to that right; do not exploit the quality or substance of news for readership or advertising gain; do not confuse sensational items with genuinely important subjects.
policy_text: News organisations must consider themselves as special socio-economic agencies whose entrepreneurial objectives have to be limited by the conditions for providing access to a fundamental right. / the media should exploit neither the quality nor the substance of the news or opinions for purposes of boosting readership or audience figures in order to increase advertising revenue. / Neither publishers and proprietors nor journalists should consider that they own the news.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Proprietorial Editorial Authority vs. Journalist Internal Freedom
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Allow publishers and proprietors to exercise full editorial control over their media organisations, including directing journalists' work in line with the owner's ideological or commercial interests.
pole_b: Protect journalists' internal freedom from proprietorial pressure; require editorial rules separate from labour law to govern publisher–journalist relations; limit owners' ideological orientations by the absolute requirements of truthful news and honest opinion; require transparency about ownership so audiences can assess potential bias.
policy_text: in addition to safeguarding the freedom of the media, freedom within the media must also be protected and internal pressures guarded against. / the legitimate respect for publishers' and owners' ideological orientations is limited by the absolute requirements on truthful news reporting and ethical opinions. / rules must be drawn up for editorial staff in order to regulate professional relations between the journalists and the publishers and proprietors within the media, separately from the normal requirements of labour relations.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Public Interest / Story Importance vs. Legal and Ethical Means of Newsgathering
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Where the public interest in a story is sufficiently important, justify the use of illegal or ethically questionable means (undercover methods, use of leaked or stolen material, deception of sources) to obtain the information.
pole_b: The ends do not justify the means in journalism; information must always be obtained by legal and ethical means, regardless of the importance or public interest value of the story.
policy_text: In the journalist's profession the end does not justify the means; therefore information must be obtained by legal and ethical means.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Media Watchdog / Agenda-Setting Role vs. Prohibition on "Mediocracy"
shared_tension_label: Watchdog scrutiny of power vs. non-substitution for public authority
pole_a: Journalism's accountability function gives it a quasi-institutional role: the media can legitimately set the public agenda, speak on behalf of public opinion, and act as a counter-authority to government and other powerful institutions.
pole_b: Media must not replace public institutions, claim to represent public opinion, or transform themselves into a "mediocracy" — an unrepresentative, unaccountable counter-authority. Journalism's legitimacy rests on serving citizens' information rights, not on wielding independent political power.
policy_text: It would be wrong to infer from the importance of this role that the media actually represent public opinion or that they should replace the specific functions of the public authorities or institutions of an educational or cultural character such as schools. / This would amount to transforming the media and journalism into authorities or counter-authorities ('mediocracy'), even though they would not be representative of the citizens or subject to the same democratic controls as the public authorities.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Source Confidentiality vs. Verification and Audience Transparency
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Prioritise full transparency about the identity and interests of sources, so audiences can evaluate the credibility and potential bias of information provided to them.
pole_b: Legally protect and expand the conscience clause and professional secrecy regarding confidential sources; do not reveal the identity of sources who provide information in confidence.
policy_text: we must legally expand and clarify the nature of the conscience clause and professional secrecy vis-a-vis confidential sources, harmonising national provisions on this matter so that they can be implemented in the wider context of democratic Europe.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Sensationalism and Audience Engagement vs. Editorial Seriousness and Accurate Headlines
shared_tension_label: Audience preference as editorial driver vs. editorial independence from demand
pole_a: Prioritise audience engagement, emotional appeal, and click-worthiness in headlines, story selection, and presentation, using sensational framing to maximise reach.
pole_b: Distinguish genuinely important subjects from merely sensational ones; ensure headlines and summaries reflect the actual substance of the underlying story; do not exploit journalistic duties to acquire personal prestige or influence; do not exploit news quality for audience or advertising gain.
policy_text: In journalism, controversial or sensational items must not be confused with subjects on which it is important to provide information. / News headlines and summaries must reflect as closely as possible the substance of the facts and data presented.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Media Independence vs. Meaningful Ethical Accountability
shared_tension_label: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
pole_a: Rely on journalists' and media organisations' internal ethics and self-governance, resisting any external oversight body's authority to review or publicise ethical failures.
pole_b: Establish formal self-regulatory bodies comprising diverse stakeholders (publishers, journalists, users, academics, judges); require media to commit in advance to publishing those bodies' resolutions; conduct and publish annual credibility research comparing published news against actual facts.
policy_text: self-regulatory bodies or mechanisms must be set up comprising publishers, journalists, media users' associations, experts from the academic world and judges; they will be responsible for issuing resolutions on respect for ethical precepts in journalism, with prior commitment on the part of the media to publish the relevant resolutions. / The self-regulatory bodies or mechanisms, the media users' associations and the relevant university departments could publish each year the research done a posteriori on the truthfulness of the information broadcast by the media, comparing the news with the actual facts.

source_name: Spain (Andalousia) Ethics of Journalism
tension_name: Publication Speed and Editorial Independence vs. Correction and Right of Reply
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Once published, treat content as final; resist correction or reply obligations as interference with editorial independence or as operationally burdensome.
pole_b: Correct false or erroneous news items and opinions automatically, speedily, and with full relevant information at the request of those affected; implement the right of reply as a harmonised entitlement across Council of Europe member states; allow for legal sanctions and compensation where appropriate.
policy_text: At the request of the persons concerned, the news media must correct, automatically and speedily, and with all relevant information provided, any news item or opinion conveyed by them which is false or erroneous. / In order to harmonise the application and exercise of this right in the member states of the Council of Europe, we must implement Resolution (74) 26 on the right of reply.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Truth-telling vs. source confidentiality
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Protect source identity absolutely, even when the source has misled the journalist or when disclosure could prevent serious harm.
pole_b: Guarantee source confidentiality as both a right and a professional duty, revealing identity only in the two narrowly defined exceptional circumstances stated in the code.
policy_text: Professional secrecy is a journalist's right, as well as a duty that guarantees the confidentiality of information sources. Consequently, journalists shall guarantee the right of their information sources to remain anonymous, if so requested.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Freedom to investigate and report vs. right to privacy
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Pursue and publish information freely, treating the public's right to know as the overriding value.
pole_b: Respect the privacy and personal image of individuals; intrude into private life only when defence of the public interest demands it, and apply tighter restrictions for hospitalised persons and minors.
policy_text: Without prejudice to protecting the right of citizens to be informed, the journalist shall respect the right of persons to their own privacy and image. … Defence of the public interest alone justifies intrusion or inquiry into a person's private life without his or her prior consent.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Comprehensive / accurate reporting vs. dignity and harm to individuals
shared_tension_label: Truth-telling and public right to know vs. harm avoidance
pole_a: Report all relevant facts fully and without omission, including expressions, images, and testimonies that may be damaging or humiliating to individuals.
pole_b: Avoid publishing expressions, images, or testimonies that are humiliating or damaging to individuals' personal status, physical integrity, or moral integrity, unless the content is strictly editorially necessary.
policy_text: In general, expressions, images or testimonies which are humiliating or damaging to the personal status of individuals and their physical or moral integrity should be avoided.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Presumption of innocence vs. public's right to know about criminal proceedings
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Report fully on persons suspected, accused, or convicted of crimes, including naming their family members and identifying victims, in order to give the public a complete account.
pole_b: Apply the presumption of innocence in all reporting on suspects and accused persons; avoid naming relatives and friends unless strictly necessary; protect victim identity, especially in sexual-offence cases; avoid coverage that causes avoidable harm.
policy_text: The journalist must embrace the principle that every person is innocent until proven otherwise and avoid as far as possible any harmful consequences resulting from the fulfilment of his or her journalistic duties.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Protection of minors vs. public interest in youth crime and safety
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Report on criminal matters and safety threats involving minors with the same investigative thoroughness applied to adult subjects, including interviews, photographs, and records.
pole_b: Apply the privacy and presumption-of-innocence criteria with "extreme rigour" when minors are involved; refrain entirely from interviewing, photographing, or recording minors in relation to criminal activities or privacy matters.
policy_text: The criteria indicated in the above two principles shall be applied with extreme rigour when the coverage may affect minors. In particular, the journalist shall refrain from interviewing, photographing or recording minors with regard to matters relating to criminal activities or those which can be considered to fall within the field of privacy.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Editorial independence vs. employer and ownership authority
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Comply with editorial direction from the media organisation, including adopting editorial stances and moral positions required by management, even when these conflict with the journalist's professional conscience.
pole_b: Invoke the conscience clause against editorial demands that damage professional dignity or substantially alter the editorial stance; resist all internal and external pressure to deviate from the ethical code; claim decent working conditions as both right and duty.
policy_text: The right to invoke the conscience clause, if the media on which they rely claims a moral attitude that damages their professional dignity or substantively alters the editorial stance.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Speed and completeness of publication vs. verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish quickly and completely, even if the origin of all facts has not been fully verified, in order to serve the public's immediate right to know.
pole_b: Report only on facts of whose origin the journalist is certain; substantiate all circulated information by comparing sources and offering the subject a right of response; promptly correct any errors in an equivalent format.
policy_text: The commitment to the search for truth shall always lead journalists to report only on facts of whose origin they are certain… They must substantiate the information they circulate, including the duty to compare sources and to give the person concerned the opportunity to offer his or her own version of the facts.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Public's right to know vs. off-the-record and right not to provide information
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Override off-the-record designations and the subject's refusal to answer when the public's right to be informed demands it.
pole_b: Honour the off-the-record rule — whether expressly invoked or inferred from the informant's intent — and respect any individual's right to decline to provide information, subject to the same exceptions as professional secrecy.
policy_text: With the same exceptions provided for professional secrecy, the journalist shall respect the off the record rule if it has been expressly invoked or it is concluded that such was the will of the informant.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Editorial viewpoint and non-neutrality vs. clear fact/opinion distinction
shared_tension_label: Factual impartiality vs. editorial opinion
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Express editorial viewpoints, interpretations, and critical opinions without necessarily maintaining a clear formal boundary between those opinions and reported facts.
pole_b: Always make a clear and unequivocal distinction between reported facts and opinions, interpretations, or conjecture — while retaining full freedom not to be neutral.
policy_text: Journalists shall always make a clear and unequivocal distinction between the facts they recount and what may be opinions, interpretations or conjecture, although in the exercise of their professional activity they are not obliged to be neutral.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Commercial and structural pressures vs. editorial integrity (paid influence, dual roles, conflicts of interest)
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept commercial arrangements — press trips, sponsored content, dual news/publicity assignments, financial interests in covered entities — as economically necessary features of journalism, especially in under-resourced outlets.
pole_b: Maintain strict separation between news and publicity; decline all third-party remuneration for editorial influence; never use privileged professional information for personal gain; abstain from covering securities in which the journalist or their family has a significant interest.
policy_text: The journalist shall not accept, directly or indirectly, remuneration or gratuities from third parties, for promoting, advising, influencing or having published information or opinions of any kind.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Investigative methods vs. lawful and justifiable newsgathering
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever methods are necessary to obtain information that serves the public interest, including deceptive, undercover, or technically unlawful methods, when no other means are available.
pole_b: Use only justifiable methods to obtain news; exclude unlawful procedures from the range of permissible newsgathering techniques.
policy_text: In the performance of their professional duties, journalists shall use justifiable methods to obtain news, which excludes unlawful procedures.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Government transparency and access to public information vs. official secrecy
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Accept government restrictions on access to public archives, administrative records, and official information when authorities invoke secrecy, national security, or administrative procedures.
pole_b: Monitor scrupulously public authorities' transparency obligations and always defend free access to public information, archives, and administrative records.
policy_text: It is the responsibility of journalists to monitor scrupulously fulfilment by the Public Authorities of their obligation of transparency of information. In particular, they shall always defend free access to information from, or generated by, these Authorities, in their Archives or Administrative Records.

source_name: Spain Code of Ethics (Federation of Press Associations of Spain)
tension_name: Digital and social-media speed and norms vs. full application of ethical standards
shared_tension_label: Consistent Platform-Neutral Standards vs. Platform-Specific Adaptation
pole_a: Treat digital and social-media journalism as operationally distinct from traditional journalism, justifying relaxed verification, correction, and distinction standards given platform speed and format constraints.
pole_b: Apply all principles and standards of the code — verification, fact/opinion distinction, correction, right of reply, privacy protections, source confidentiality — equally and without exception to digital and technological formats.
policy_text: The principles and standards contained in this Code of Ethics shall also apply in cases where journalists make use of digital or other technological communication or information systems in any format.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Speed and completeness of disclosure vs. verification and known-origin publishing
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish promptly and fully — including unverified or unattributed material — so that newsworthy information reaches the public without delay.
pole_b: Publish only material whose origin is known; clearly label any information that is unconfirmed; report all essential elements only when the journalist can stand behind them.
policy_text: Not to publish information, documents, images or sound recordings of which the origin is unknown to the journalist. / If information is unconfirmed to clearly say so. / Not to suppress information or any essential elements of a story.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Truth-seeking and full disclosure vs. privacy protection
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: Report every true and newsworthy fact about a person, including details drawn from their private life, on the ground that the public has a right to know.
pole_b: Respect people's privacy and disregard anonymous or unfounded accusations; intrude on private life only when genuine public interest demands it.
policy_text: To respect peoples' privacy in so far as the public interest does not demand otherwise. / To disregard anonymous or unfounded accusations. / To seek out the truth, in the interests of the public's right to know, whatever the consequences to him- or herself.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Truth-seeking and full disclosure vs. human dignity, victim sensitivity, and non-discrimination
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Report the full, unfiltered reality of suffering, violence, or personal characteristics because accurate depiction — however graphic or categorically descriptive — serves the public's right to know.
pole_b: Report in ways that respect human dignity: avoid discriminatory allusions to personal characteristics unless clearly relevant; handle images and accounts of suffering so as to respect victims and their loved ones.
policy_text: In respecting human dignity, the journalist must avoid any allusion by text, image or sound to a person's ethnic or national origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation as well as to any illness or physical or mental handicap that could be discriminatory in character. / The reporting of war, acts of terrorism, accidents and catastrophes by means of text, image and sound should respect the victims' suffering and the feelings of their loved ones.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Investigative necessity vs. honest and non-manipulative information-gathering methods
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Use whatever methods — including deception, concealment of identity, or entrapment — when they are the only realistic means of obtaining information that is genuinely in the public interest.
pole_b: Use only honest, legitimate methods to obtain information; do not manipulate gathered material or have it manipulated with a view to falsification.
policy_text: Not to use dishonest methods to obtain information, recordings, images or documents. / Not to manipulate them, or have them manipulated by a third party with a view to falsification.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. story credibility, truth-seeking, and public-interest disclosure
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Identify confidential sources when doing so would significantly strengthen a story's credibility, reveal information essential to the public interest, or is itself newsworthy.
pole_b: Respect professional secrecy absolutely; never reveal the identity of a source who provided information in confidence.
policy_text: To respect professional secrecy and not reveal the source of any information obtained in confidence.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Duty of editorial obedience vs. right of conscience-based and policy-based refusal
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Follow all editorial directives from designated superiors as a matter of professional hierarchy and employment obligation.
pole_b: Refuse any directive that contradicts this Declaration's principles, the journalist's professional conscience, or the organisation's previously stated written policy; suffer no prejudice for doing so.
policy_text: To take journalistic directives only from designated editorial superiors; and to respect those directives only when they are not contrary to this declaration. / The right not to act in any way nor express any opinion that is contrary to professional rules or personal conscience. As a result, journalists should not suffer any prejudice.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Public responsibility as primary obligation vs. loyalty to employers and public authorities
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Give primary weight to the interests of the employing organisation or to directions from public authorities when they conflict with the public's right to be informed.
pole_b: Responsibility to the public must come before any responsibility to employers or public authorities; this hierarchy is foundational and is not overridden by institutional loyalty.
policy_text: Journalists' responsibility to the public must come before any they bear towards a third party, notably employers and public authorities.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Commercial and ownership pressures vs. editorial independence
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Accept advantages, advertiser conditions, or commercial arrangements that bring resources or convenience to the journalist or outlet, even if they place implicit limits on editorial choices.
pole_b: Reject any advantage or promise that could limit professional independence; avoid all forms of commercial advertising activity; claim the right to know who owns the outlet; ensure economic independence through appropriate remuneration.
policy_text: Not to accept any advantage nor any promise that could limit his or her professional independence or expression of opinion. / To avoid as journalists any form of commercial advertising; and never to accept conditions laid down by advertisers directly or indirectly. / The right to transparency as to the ownership of the company for which the journalist works. / An appropriate remuneration… should ensure his or her economic independence.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
shared_tension_label: Self-regulation and press autonomy vs. external legal and state accountability
pole_a: Accept state regulation, legal mechanisms, or official-body oversight as legitimate and sometimes necessary constraints on journalistic conduct.
pole_b: Accept only the judgment of professional colleagues, the Press Council, or legitimate professional ethics organisations; reject any interference by the state or other official bodies in journalistic regulation.
policy_text: journalists only accept the judgment of their professional colleagues, the Press Council or legitimate organizations of professional ethics. They reject any interference by the state or other official bodies.

source_name: Switzerland Declaration of Duties and Rights of Journalists (Declaration of Duties + Declaration of Rights + Preface)
tension_name: Transparency about errors and Press Council rulings vs. reputational and editorial interests of the outlet
shared_tension_label: Institutional Reputation vs. Transparent and Prominent Error Correction
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Decline to publish corrections or Press Council rulings when doing so would damage the outlet's reputation, re-publicise harmful material, or undermine editorial authority.
pole_b: Rectify all published factual errors; publish at minimum a short summary of any Press Council decision concerning one's own outlet; treat transparency about mistakes as a journalistic obligation rather than a discretionary act of humility.
policy_text: To rectify any published information that is revealed to be factually incorrect. / Fair reporting requires at least a short, published summary of a Press Council decision in relation to one's own media.

source_name: Time Warner/CNN News Group, Journalistic Integrity / Freedom of Expression / Diversity of Viewpoints / Responsible Content policy
tension_name: Speed of publication vs. pre-publication verification
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Publish or broadcast content as quickly as possible to meet competitive and audience expectations, even before all facts are fully confirmed.
pole_b: Confirm all facts before any online article or television segment is released to the public.
policy_text: We expect our reporters, producers and writers to be fair and honest and to confirm the facts before online articles or TV segments are released to the public.

source_name: Time Warner/CNN News Group, Journalistic Integrity / Freedom of Expression / Diversity of Viewpoints / Responsible Content policy
tension_name: Editorial independence from external interference vs. internal institutional ethical mandates
shared_tension_label: Editorial Authority vs. Journalist's Conscience
pole_a: Journalists operate entirely free from any outside direction — including direction from their own employer — in determining what to report and how.
pole_b: Journalists must be free from interference by governments and external actors, but must simultaneously abide by the high ethical standards and integrity requirements set by the company.
policy_text: Journalists must resist government and external interference in their reporting, while simultaneously complying with the company's own ethical and integrity standards — a distinction the code draws but does not fully reconcile.

source_name: Time Warner/CNN News Group, Journalistic Integrity / Freedom of Expression / Diversity of Viewpoints / Responsible Content policy
tension_name: Social-impact editorial agenda vs. journalistic neutrality
shared_tension_label: Advocacy journalism vs. objectivity and neutrality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Journalists report facts and tell stories without a predetermined agenda about which social issues deserve elevation or what the desired cultural impact should be.
pole_b: Use entertainment and creative programming deliberately and intentionally to elevate dialogue on important social issues and generate positive cultural and social impact.
policy_text: We understand that our entertainment programming can have an impact on culture. Below are recent examples of the ways in which we have elevated the dialogue on important social issues through our creative programming and initiatives.

source_name: Toronto Platform for Action on Women and Media (UNESCO Symposium)
tension_name: Advocacy role of media vs. preservation of press freedom
shared_tension_label: Advocacy journalism vs. objectivity and neutrality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Media maintains editorial neutrality and independence, refraining from using its platforms as instruments of advocacy for any social cause, including gender equality.
pole_b: Media actively uses communication as a driving force promoting women's equal and active participation in development, while simultaneously preserving freedom of expression and freedom of the press.
policy_text: To use communication as a driving force in the promotion of women's active and equal participation in development in a context of peace and equality, while preserving freedom of expression and freedom of the press.

source_name: Toronto Platform for Action on Women and Media (UNESCO Symposium)
tension_name: Monitoring discriminatory media content vs. freedom of expression and press freedom
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Any monitoring mechanism for media content risks censorship and must not be established, since the identification and suppression of "discriminatory" images necessarily implicates editorial judgment that should remain free from external oversight.
pole_b: Monitoring mechanisms should be established to identify images that are discriminatory or that violate women's and children's rights across all media formats — including online, advertising, marketing, and entertainment — provided such mechanisms are anchored in human rights and dignity rather than censorship.
policy_text: Urge the definition of ethical guidelines adapted to all types of media, including on-line technologies and virtual reality, as well as monitoring mechanisms with respect to images that are discriminatory or that violate children's and women's rights in information, advertisements, marketing, and entertainment; this not with a mind to restrain freedom of expression and of the press, but rather to ensure the respect of human rights and dignity.

source_name: Toronto Platform for Action on Women and Media (UNESCO Symposium)
tension_name: Affirmative structural intervention for gender equity vs. editorial and hiring autonomy
shared_tension_label: Union/collective organisation vs. individual editorial autonomy
pole_a: Media organisations retain full autonomy over hiring, promotion, compensation, and editorial composition decisions based on merit, seniority, or market forces, without external mandates specifying targets, timetables, or proportional representation requirements.
pole_b: Media organisations should adopt positive action programmes including equal pay, fair promotion procedures, concrete targets and timetables for women in decision-making positions, equal opportunity employer declarations, removal of gender and marital status from job applications, action against sexual harassment, and gender-parity requirements in regulatory and self-regulatory bodies.
policy_text: Adopt positive action programmes, including equal pay for equal work, equal access to training, fair and transparent promotion procedures, targets and timetables to achieve a fair proportion of women in decision-making positions, action against sexual harassment, so that women can reach their full potential as media professionals.

source_name: Toronto Platform for Action on Women and Media (UNESCO Symposium)
tension_name: Responsible/accurate representation of women vs. commercial and entertainment freedom
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Media and entertainment enterprises exercise full creative and commercial discretion over content, including the use of sexualised images of women, stereotyped portrayals, and dramatic treatment of violence against women, as audience demand and commercial imperatives direct.
pole_b: Media must reject negative, stereotyped, and degrading images of women; must not use women's bodies as sex objects; must not portray violence against women as entertainment; and must develop editorial policies, guidelines, and gender-awareness training to ensure accurate, diverse, and dignified representation of women across all content.
policy_text: Even more insidious are the use by media of women's bodies as sex objects, and violence against women as 'entertainment'. / the present global situation in the media shows the perpetuation and re-enforcement of negative images of women that do not provide an accurate or realistic picture of women's multiple roles and contributions to a changing world.

source_name: Toronto Platform for Action on Women and Media (UNESCO Symposium)
tension_name: Condemning extremism vs. media pluralism and protection of controversial speech
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Media maintains pluralistic openness to all political and religious viewpoints, including those that others characterise as extremist, as a necessary condition of press freedom and democratic discourse.
pole_b: Media should actively condemn all types of extremism — especially religious extremism — that jeopardises women's rights and democracy, and should monitor and denounce attacks on media professionals who expose or speak out against extremists.
policy_text: Condemn all types of extremism, in particular religious extremism, which jeopardizes the rights of women and democracy. / Monitor and denounce attacks on media professionals or users who expose or speak out against extremists, be they political, religious, racist, etc.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Press freedom advocacy vs. editorial/political independence
shared_tension_label: Advocacy journalism vs. objectivity and neutrality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Journalists maintain strict editorial neutrality and refrain from taking active political stances, including on press-freedom issues, in order not to compromise perceived independence.
pole_b: Journalists actively and openly protest any restriction on freedom of communication imposed by legislators, institutions, or individuals, at all times and in all places.
policy_text: Promising with our free will to protest against the restrictions by The Legislator or other institutions and persons on Freedom of Communication, anytime and everywhere;

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Public right to information vs. protection of private life
shared_tension_label: Privacy of individuals vs. public interest and accountability
pole_a: The public's right to receive information and learn the facts takes priority; journalists publish accurate information about individuals whenever it is newsworthy, including details of private life.
pole_b: Individuals' private lives are shielded from publication; the default is protection of privacy, with publication permitted only when the public interest requires it.
policy_text: The private life of individuals shall not be the subject of publication, except when required due to the public interests. / The public's right to receive information and the right to learn the facts are under protection.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Watchdog/accountability reporting vs. presumption of innocence
shared_tension_label: Public's right to know vs. presumption of innocence
pole_a: Investigative journalism serves the public interest by exposing suspected wrongdoing before courts act; journalists report credible evidence of criminal conduct, attribute conduct to named individuals on reasonable grounds, and let the public draw conclusions.
pole_b: No person is declared "guilty" until a judicial determination is made; criminal acts are attributed to individuals only when reasonable grounds exist; reporting does not pre-judge outcomes.
policy_text: No one shall be declared 'guilty' unless it is determined by the judicial system. / Acts considered as crime according to the law cannot be attributed to anyone unless there are reasonable reasons to believe that it is true.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Timeliness vs. verification before publication
shared_tension_label: Speed of publication vs. verification
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Journalists publish news as quickly as possible to satisfy the public's right to timely information and to meet publication-date obligations, even when full verification has not been completed.
pole_b: News that can be investigated within the boundaries of journalism must not be published until its accuracy has been verified; the publication-date record is respected, but not at the expense of verification.
policy_text: The news which can be investigated within the boundaries of journalism shall not be published without being investigated or without being sure of their accuracy. / The time record set for the date of publication shall be respected.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Source confidentiality vs. accuracy and the public interest in not being misled
shared_tension_label: Source transparency vs. Source confidentiality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Source confidentiality is absolute; journalists never reveal a source's identity regardless of the source's conduct or motives.
pole_b: Journalists protect source confidentiality as a default; however, when a source is using the journalist's protection to deliberately mislead the public for personal, political, or similar reasons, the confidentiality obligation may be lifted.
policy_text: The journalist protects the confidentiality of his/her sources. An exception are cases where a source aims to mislead the public due to personal, political and similar causes.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Investigative/critical reporting vs. dignity and non-humiliation norms
shared_tension_label: Fair and transparent newsgathering vs. undercover / public-interest investigation
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Investigative journalism necessarily exposes, shames, and publicly damages the reputations of wrongdoers; the watchdog function requires reporting that may feel humiliating or degrading to its subjects.
pole_b: Criticism is legitimate but must remain within limits; statements that humiliate, degrade, or sully individuals or organisations beyond the limits of criticism are prohibited; non-discrimination on protected characteristics is absolute.
policy_text: Statements that are humiliating, degrading or sullying individuals and organizations beyond the limits of criticism shall not be allowed. / No one shall be condemned or humiliated because of his/her race, gender, age, health, physical and mental disability, social level and religious beliefs.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Right of reply vs. editorial independence
shared_tension_label: Right of reply and fairness vs. speed and editorial control of publication
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Subjects of critical reporting may use the right of reply to pressure or suppress legitimate journalism; unconstrained reply rights undermine editorial independence and enable powerful actors to flood coverage with rebuttals.
pole_b: Press organs respect and uphold the right of individuals and organisations to reply to and denounce incorrect publications; this right is a due-process safeguard and a correction mechanism.
policy_text: The press organs respect the right to reply and denounce regarding the wrong publications.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Full factual reporting vs. avoidance of violent/hateful content
shared_tension_label: Full and accurate reporting vs. decency / restraint in depicting violence, sex, and distress
pole_a: Accurate reporting of real-world events — wars, atrocities, hate crimes, extremist movements — requires depicting and quoting violent, hateful, or discriminatory content as it actually exists.
pole_b: Journalists avoid publishing content that is violent, hateful, tyrannical, or encouraging of discrimination, or that harms humanitarian values, regardless of its news value.
policy_text: The journalist avoids publishing which is violent, hateful, tyrannical and encouraging discrimination, and harming humanitarian values.

source_name: Turkey — Professional Principles of the Press (MCDA)
tension_name: Editorial integrity vs. commercial pressure (advertising labelling)
shared_tension_label: Editorial Independence vs. Commercial and Advertising Pressures
pole_a: Commercial pressures lead journalists or outlets to present sponsored, advertorial, or native-advertising content in formats indistinguishable from editorial content, blurring the boundary for audiences.
pole_b: All content that is commercial in nature (announcements, advertisements) is clearly labelled so that no reader or viewer can doubt its commercial provenance; editorial and commercial content are strictly distinguishable.
policy_text: These qualifications of publications, which are announcements and advertisements in nature, are stated in a way that leaves no room for doubt.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Active anti-racism advocacy vs. journalistic neutrality/objectivity
shared_tension_label: Advocacy journalism vs. objectivity and neutrality
tension_group: truth and accountability to the public
pole_a: Journalists maintain neutrality and balance, treating racism and racial discrimination as contested political questions to which they do not take sides — presenting "both sides" without editorial orientation toward eradication.
pole_b: Journalists and mass media actively use their platform to promote understanding, tolerance, and friendship among racial and ethnic groups, and explicitly contribute to the eradication of racism, racial discrimination, and racial prejudice, refusing to present stereotyped, partial, unilateral, or tendentious pictures of individuals or groups.
policy_text: The mass media and those who control or serve them, as well as all organized groups within national communities, are urged—with due regard to the principles embodied in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, particularly the principle of freedom of expression—to promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among individuals and groups and to contribute to the eradication of racism, racial discrimination and racial prejudice, in particular by refraining from presenting a stereotyped, partial, unilateral or tendentious picture of individuals and of various human groups.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Press freedom to report racial-superiority claims vs. duty to refuse their propagation
shared_tension_label: Freedom of expression and fair comment vs. harm prevention (hatred / discrimination)
pole_a: Journalists report and amplify theories claiming racial or ethnic superiority or inferiority — including those dressed in scientific language — on the grounds that the marketplace of ideas and freedom of expression require that all views receive airing.
pole_b: Journalists reject, refuse to propagate, and decline to lend credibility to any theory claiming that racial or ethnic groups are inherently superior or inferior, or that bases value judgments on racial differentiation, on the grounds that such theories have no scientific foundation and are contrary to the moral and ethical principles of humanity; they further support the principle that law may legitimately curb such propaganda.
policy_text: Any theory which involves the claim that racial or ethnic groups are inherently superior or inferior, thus implying that some would be entitled to dominate or eliminate others, presumed to be inferior, or which bases value judgments on racial differentiation, has no scientific foundation and is contrary to the moral and ethical principles of humanity.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Structural/systemic framing of racism vs. event-driven or individualist framing
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Journalists cover racism as individual acts of overt hatred or discrete discriminatory incidents, treating each event as isolated without reference to structural arrangements, institutionalised practices, or systemic racial inequality.
pole_b: Journalists understand and convey racism in its full scope — encompassing racist ideologies, prejudiced attitudes, discriminatory behaviour, structural arrangements, and institutionalised practices resulting in racial inequality — and attribute differences in group achievement to geographical, historical, political, economic, social, and cultural factors rather than to inherent group characteristics.
policy_text: Racism includes racist ideologies, prejudiced attitudes, discriminatory behavior, structural arrangements and institutionalized practices resulting in racial inequality as well as the fallacious notion that discriminatory relations between groups are morally and scientifically justifiable; it is reflected in discriminatory provisions in legislation or regulations and discriminatory practices as well as in anti-social beliefs and acts.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Affirmative reciprocal sourcing obligation vs. editorial gatekeeping discretion
shared_tension_label: Affirmative reciprocal sourcing obligation vs. editorial gatekeeping discretion
pole_a: Journalists and editors exercise conventional gatekeeping discretion in selecting sources and story angles, resulting in coverage that systematically foregrounds some racial or ethnic groups while others are structurally excluded from expressing themselves fully or at all.
pole_b: Journalists ensure that communication between racial and ethnic groups is a genuinely reciprocal process, that each group can express itself and be fully heard without hindrance, and that mass media are freely receptive to ideas facilitating inter-group communication — including ideas that editorial convenience or majority-audience preference might otherwise suppress.
policy_text: Communication between racial and ethnic groups must be a reciprocal process, enabling them to express themselves and to be fully heard without let or hindrance. The mass media should therefore be freely receptive to ideas of individuals and groups which facilitate such communication.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Framing remedial measures for disadvantaged groups as justified vs. framing them as discriminatory
shared_tension_label: Framing remedial measures for disadvantaged groups as justified vs. framing them as discriminatory
pole_a: Journalists report special programmes, affirmative policies, or positive measures targeting disadvantaged racial or ethnic groups as instances of reverse discrimination or preferential treatment, applying a formal-equality frame that treats all racial groups as already equivalent in social position.
pole_b: Journalists report special programmes for socially or economically disadvantaged racial or ethnic groups as legitimate remedial measures necessary to achieve substantive equality, consistent with the principle that equal footing in dignity and rights requires affirmative action where circumstances warrant, and that the existence of anti-discrimination law alone is insufficient.
policy_text: Where circumstances warrant, special programmes should be undertaken to promote the advancement of disadvantaged groups and, in the case of nationals, to ensure their effective participation in the decision-making processes of the community.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Accurate complexity in reporting race science vs. simplification demands of popular media
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Journalists simplify and abbreviate scientific findings on race for popular audiences, stripping contextual and methodological nuance in ways that predictably produce misinterpretation — presenting contested findings as settled, or settled refutations as contested.
pole_b: Journalists reporting on race-related research take responsibility for ensuring findings are not misinterpreted, actively communicate the interdisciplinary scientific consensus (that all peoples have equal intellectual and social potential and that achievement differences are attributable to contextual factors), and decline to present racial-hierarchy research as though it represents legitimate scientific controversy.
policy_text: It is, in particular, incumbent upon such specialists to ensure, by all means available to them, that their research findings are not misinterpreted, and also that they assist the public in understanding such findings.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Framing migration as contribution and dignity vs. security/economic-burden framing
shared_tension_label: National cultural and linguistic protection vs. critical journalistic independence
pole_a: Journalists frame coverage of migrant workers and communities primarily in terms of security risks, economic costs, or cultural threat to the host society, without acknowledging migrant contributions to development or their human rights entitlements.
pole_b: Journalists ensure that coverage of migrant workers and communities of foreign origin reflects their contributions to the host country's development, their entitlement to security, respect for dignity, and cultural values, and the particular needs of their children (including mother-tongue education), consistent with the Declaration's requirement of reciprocal communication and dignified treatment.
policy_text: Population groups of foreign origin, particularly migrant workers and their families who contribute to the development of the host country, should benefit from appropriate measures designed to afford them security and respect for their dignity and cultural values and to facilitate their adaptation to the host environment and their professional advancement with a view to their subsequent reintegration in their country of origin and their contribution to its development.

source_name: UNESCO Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice (1978)
tension_name: Personal journalist duty to combat racism vs. professional detachment norm
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Journalists maintain professional detachment and understand their role as neutral conveyors of information, treating racism and racial discrimination as external phenomena to be reported rather than as issues in which they bear individual ethical responsibility.
pole_b: Journalists recognise that as human beings they are individually obligated — not merely permitted — to promote harmony among peoples, to combat racism and racial prejudice, and to assist by every available means in eradicating racial discrimination in all its forms; this personal duty coexists with and shapes their professional conduct.
policy_text: They are accordingly under an obligation to promote harmony among the peoples, to combat racism and racial prejudice and to assist by every means available to them in eradicating racial discrimination in all its forms.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Child protection from harm vs. public interest / newsworthiness
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Publish a story about or involving an individual child because it is highly newsworthy or serves the public interest, accepting that some potential harm to the child may result.
pole_b: Withhold or substantially alter a story — including one that is highly newsworthy — whenever it might put the child, siblings, or peers at risk, even potential risk, and when doubt about that risk exists, default to reporting on the general situation rather than the individual child.
policy_text: Do not publish a story or an image which might put the child, siblings or peers at risk even when identities are changed, obscured or not used. / When in doubt about whether a child is at risk, report on the general situation for children rather than on an individual child, no matter how newsworthy the story.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Child privacy and anonymity vs. child's right to be heard / autonomous voice
shared_tension_label: Child's right to be heard vs. protection from exposure
pole_a: Give the child a voice — allow the child to speak and be identified in ways that let their perspective reach the public, even at some risk to privacy or safety.
pole_b: Protect child privacy and confidentiality as the default; give weight to child views through the reporting without necessarily exposing identity or personal detail.
policy_text: special attention is to be paid to each child's right to privacy and confidentiality, to have their opinions heard, to participate in decisions affecting them and to be protected from harm and retribution. / In certain cases, using a child's identity – their name and/or recognisable image – is in the child's best interests.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Mandatory anonymisation vs. identity use in the child's best interests
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Use the child's real name and recognisable image when editorially justified — e.g., to maximise impact, serve accountability, or honour the child's own wishes.
pole_b: Mandatory anonymisation is the default for defined categories (sexual abuse victims, perpetrators of abuse, HIV status, criminal charges/conviction); identity use is permitted only in narrow, affirmatively justified circumstances serving the child's own best interests.
policy_text: Always change the name and obscure the visual identity of any child who is identified as: a. A victim of sexual abuse or exploitation; b. A perpetrator of physical or sexual abuse; c. HIV positive, living with AIDS or has died from AIDS [unless fully informed consent]; d. Charged or convicted of a crime. / In certain cases, using a child's identity – their name and/or recognisable image – is in the child's best interests.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Child safety from contextual identification vs. accurate contextualisation of the story
shared_tension_label: Protecting children vs. public's right to full information
pole_a: Provide full geographic, community, and circumstantial context to make the story accurate, credible, and meaningful to audiences.
pole_b: Omit or obscure geographic, community, or circumstantial details that would endanger or adversely affect the child, even if those details would otherwise be standard journalistic context.
policy_text: Ensure that the child would not be endangered or adversely affected by showing their home, community or general whereabouts. / Always provide an accurate context for the child's story or image.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Child's own views and agency vs. guardian consent and adult mediation
shared_tension_label: Child's own views and agency vs. guardian consent and adult mediation
pole_a: Treat guardian consent as the operative gate for all reporting on children; accept guardian decisions as final.
pole_b: Give genuine weight to the child's own views, calibrated to age and maturity, while also obtaining guardian consent; recognise that the child's views and the guardian's consent are both required and may conflict.
policy_text: When trying to determine the best interests of a child, the child's right to have their views taken into account are to be given due weight in accordance with their age and maturity. / Obtain permission from the child and his or her guardian for all interviews, videotaping and, when possible, for documentary photographs.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Do-no-harm in interviewing vs. journalistic pursuit of truth through probing questions
shared_tension_label: Truth-seeking vs. minimising harm to children
pole_a: Ask thorough, probing, and sometimes uncomfortable questions of child interviewees to obtain accurate and complete information, accepting that some questions may cause discomfort or emotional distress.
pole_b: Avoid any questions, attitudes, or comments that are judgmental, culturally insensitive, dangerous, humiliating, or that reactivate a child's pain and grief from traumatic events, even if this limits the depth or accuracy of the account obtained.
policy_text: Do no harm to any child; avoid questions, attitudes or comments that are judgmental, insensitive to cultural values, that place a child in danger or expose a child to humiliation, or that reactivate a child's pain and grief from traumatic events.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Anti-stigmatisation vs. accurate and precise description
shared_tension_label: Completeness / Accuracy vs. Anti-Discrimination in Identity Reporting
pole_a: Use precise, descriptive labels and categorisations in reporting because accuracy and specificity are fundamental journalistic values, even if some labels carry social stigma.
pole_b: Avoid categorisations or descriptions that expose a child to negative reprisals, discrimination, lifelong abuse, or community rejection — prioritise harm prevention in language choices over maximum descriptive precision.
policy_text: Do not further stigmatise any child; avoid categorisations or descriptions that expose a child to negative reprisals – including additional physical or psychological harm, or to lifelong abuse, discrimination or rejection by their local communities.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Individual child safety vs. public accountability for child perpetrators and defendants
shared_tension_label: Full and transparent crime reporting vs. protecting vulnerable identities
pole_a: Name and identify child perpetrators or defendants in the interests of public accountability, deterrence, or transparency in the criminal justice system.
pole_b: Mandatory anonymisation of all children charged with or convicted of a crime, and all children identified as perpetrators of physical or sexual abuse — public accountability concerns do not create exceptions.
policy_text: Always change the name and obscure the visual identity of any child who is identified as: b. A perpetrator of physical or sexual abuse / d. Charged or convicted of a crime.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Precautionary default to general reporting vs. individual child's right to be heard
shared_tension_label: Child's right to be heard vs. protection from exposure
pole_a: Report on the individual child's story even when some uncertainty about risk exists, because individual testimony is more powerful, credible, and rights-respecting than generalised reporting.
pole_b: When doubt exists about whether a child is at risk, default to reporting on the general situation for children rather than on the individual child, regardless of newsworthiness.
policy_text: When in doubt about whether a child is at risk, report on the general situation for children rather than on an individual child, no matter how newsworthy the story.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Authentic account / no staging vs. narrative reconstruction for journalistic clarity
shared_tension_label: Authentic account / no staging vs. narrative reconstruction for journalistic clarity
pole_a: Reconstruct scenes or ask children to re-enact or narrate events in ways that are illustrative or clarifying, even if those events are not precisely "their own history" in a strict sense — a common practice in features and documentary journalism.
pole_b: Allow children to tell only their own authentic story or take actions that are genuinely part of their own history; no staging, reconstruction, or scripted narration.
policy_text: No staging: Do not ask children to tell a story or take an action that is not part of their own history.

source_name: UNICEF Reporting on Children Principles (Sections I–III)
tension_name: Corroboration requirement vs. credibility and primacy of child testimony
shared_tension_label: Corroboration requirement vs. credibility and primacy of child testimony
pole_a: Accept a child's account as credible testimony in its own right, as one would an adult's, and publish it without requiring independent corroboration — especially when the child is the primary witness.
pole_b: Confirm the accuracy of what a child says by seeking independent corroboration — preferably from both other children and an adult — before publishing.
policy_text: Confirm the accuracy of what the child has to say, either with other children or an adult, preferably with both.
